tasks.notes:
# Task #38 — src/commands/task.ts agent-facing usage strings

## Changes

`src/commands/task.ts`:
1. All ~20 agent-facing `ralph task <subcommand>: ...` error/validation strings renamed to
   `cairn task <subcommand>: ...` via a scoped sed (`s/`ralph task /`cairn task /g` and the
   single-quoted variant for the two `stderr.write('ralph task add: ...')` literal-string calls).
   Covers `start`, `complete`, `note`, `set-status`, `add` (including the two literal-string
   validation-failed messages), `show`, `next-id`.
2. Imported `BRAND` from `../brand` and changed the `task` subcommand group description at
   (now) line 341 from the hardcoded `'Manage tasks in .ralph/tasks.json'` to
   `` `Manage tasks in ${BRAND.dataDir}/tasks.json` `` — renders `Manage tasks in .cairn/tasks.json`.
   Per CLAUDE.md's standing CREATE-vs-RESOLVE rule this is fine: it's a static description string,
   not a path resolved against an existing project's on-disk layout.
3. Verified via `grep -in ralph src/commands/task.ts` → zero hits after the change.

## TDD

Per PERSONAL INSTRUCTIONS (test → see it fail → make it pass):
- The three existing `ralph task add`/`ralph task next-id` assertions in
  `test/commands/task.test.ts` were updated in lockstep with the source sed (same `cairn task`
  literal), so they track the source change rather than being written blind.
- Added a **new** test (`registerTaskCommands` describe block, case 10a) exercising the
  Commander wiring directly — instantiates a fresh `Command()`, calls `registerTaskCommands`,
  finds the `task` subcommand, and asserts its `.description()` is exactly
  `'Manage tasks in .cairn/tasks.json'`. This is net-new coverage: no prior test exercised
  `registerTaskCommands`'s wiring at all, only the underlying `task*` functions directly. Ran

# Task #40 — Remaining src/ rename sweep

## Source changes

**src/commands/edit.ts**
- `case 'config'` was `path.join(projectRoot, 'ralph.json')` — a hardcoded literal used to
  RESOLVE an existing file. Replaced with `findConfigFile(projectRoot)`. This was a **real bug**,
  not just a rename: on a project already on `cairn.json`, `ralph edit config` printed
  "File not found" and exited 1. Now it resolves cairn.json → legacy ralph.json → cairn.json,
  matching the standing rule in CLAUDE.md.
- Usage string: `'Usage: ralph edit [tasks|plan|config]'` → `` `Usage: ${BRAND.name} edit ...` ``.

**src/commands/status.ts** — the two user-visible hints called out in the task description:
- `"Not initialized. Run 'ralph init' first."` → `` `... Run '${BRAND.name} init' first.` ``
- `"No tasks.json found. Run 'ralph plan' to create one."` → `${BRAND.name} plan`

**src/index.ts**
- `.name('ralph')` → `.name(BRAND.name)`
- `.version(\`ralph ${CAIRN_VERSION}\`)` → `` `${BRAND.name} ${CAIRN_VERSION}` ``
- init `.description('Initialize Ralph in the current project')` → `${BRAND.displayName}`
- Line 38's comment about resolving to `.ralph/` is an accurate description of task #32's
  dual-read plumbing — left as-is.

**src/stream-filter.ts**
- ntfy titles `'Ralph'` and `` `Ralph - ${statusTitle}` `` → `BRAND.displayName`.
- Two doc comments referenced `lib/ralph_stream_filter.py`. That file was **deleted** from the
  repo (confirmed via `git log --diff-filter=D`), so the reference is dead either way — renaming
  it to `cairn_stream_filter.py` would name a file that never existed. Dropped the references

  `processStream` doc comment lost its "Matches the main loop in ... exactly" line.

**src/file-lock.ts**
- Lock-timeout error: `"...if no other ralph process is running."` → `${BRAND.name}`.
  User-facing — this is what someone sees when a stuck writer blocks the tasks file.

**src/commands/run.ts** (the task description explicitly scoped run.ts's `'ralph plan'` hint;
I also took the three adjacent branding strings since they are the same one-line class of change
and #46's verification sweep would otherwise flag them):
- `'tasks.json not found. Create it first with \'ralph plan\''` → `${BRAND.name} plan`
- `'Ralph Execution Loop Started: ...'` (iterations.log header) → `${BRAND.displayName}`
- `deps.log('Ralph Execution Loop Completed')` → `${BRAND.displayName}`
- `ntfyTitle = 'Ralph - Complete' : 'Ralph - Stopped'` → `${BRAND.displayName} - ...`
- Two doc comments "Ports build_system_prompt()/run_claude() from ralph_execute.sh" — same
  situation as stream-filter: `lib/ralph_execute.sh` is deleted. Dropped the dead provenance.

**src/process.ts** — "ported from ralph_execute.sh lines 1-29" → "Process lifecycle management
for spawned agent processes." (Same deleted-file reasoning.)

**src/tasks-file.ts** (2 comments), **src/task-counter.ts** (2 comments) — prose
"Ralph agent shells `ralph task ...`" / "separate `ralph` processes" → Cairn/cairn.

**No changes needed:** `src/commands/logs.ts` (already fully on `findTempFilePath`),
`src/commands/summarize.ts`, `src/commands/plan.ts` (zero `ralph` hits, case-insensitive),
`src/task-selector.ts` and `src/task-archiver.ts` (their only hits are comments *describing*
the intentional `.ralph_` legacy fallback — accurate, category-1 per task #46).

## Deliberately left alone

- **`src/commands/narrate.ts`**: `/tmp/ralph-tts.pid`, `/tmp/ralph-tts.sock`, and the
  `ralph_narrate_server.py` / `ralph_narrate.py` script paths. These belong to task **#41**
  (the `git mv` of the Python files must be atomic with the path updates) and task **#48**
  (socket-path branding strategy). Same for run.ts:406/413/453.
  I added a note to task **#48** flagging that `/tmp/ralph-tts.pid` is *not* in #48's
  description but must migrate together with the socket — a cairn socket paired with a ralph
  pid file would orphan a running server's PID file.
- All `.ralph_`/`.ralph/` legacy-fallback comments and logic (tasks #32/#33 work). Not reverted.
- Everything on the exclusion list. No historical-record file was touched.

## TDD (red → green, per PERSONAL INSTRUCTIONS)

Tests were written/updated first and confirmed failing (**13 fail**) against unmodified source,
then the source was changed to make them pass.

- `test/index.test.ts` — name → `'cairn'`, version → `'cairn 0.1.0'` (2 places).
  **New test**: `init command description names the current brand, not the legacy one` —
  asserts the init description contains `Cairn` and *not* `Ralph`.
- `test/commands/status.test.ts` — the two existing tests only asserted on the substrings
  `'Not initialized'` / `'No tasks.json found'`, which pass regardless of the command hint.
  Tightened both to assert the exact hint (`Run 'cairn init' first.` / `Run 'cairn plan' to
  create one.`) plus a negative assertion against the old text. Without this the rename was
  literally untested.
- `test/commands/edit.test.ts` — renamed the config test to expect `cairn.json`, and added **two
  new tests** covering the resolution bug: `resolves an existing legacy ralph.json` and
  `prefers cairn.json when both config files exist`. Usage assertion → `Usage: cairn edit`.
- `test/stream-filter.test.ts` — three ntfy title assertions → `Cairn`, `Cairn - Finished`,
  `Cairn - Failed`.
- `test/file-lock.test.ts` — **new test (4)**: holds a fresh lock, then stubs `Date.now` so the
  first retry lands past the deadline (call 1 returns t0 so `deadline = t0 + 15000`; later calls
  return `t0 + 20000`, which is still under the 60s stale threshold so the lock is not broken).
  Asserts the thrown message says `no other cairn process is running`. Runs in ~0ms instead of
  the real 15s wait. Old test (4) renumbered to (5).
- `test/commands/run.test.ts` — iterations.log header assertion → `'Cairn Execution Loop
  Started'`; the tasks.json-missing test now also asserts `Create it first with 'cairn plan'`;
  the tada-tags test now also asserts `title: 'Cairn - Complete'`. **Two new tests**:
  `completion ntfy title uses the current brand when the loop stops early` (covers the
  `Cairn - Stopped` branch, previously untested) and `final summary banner names the current
  brand` (asserts `'Cairn Execution Loop Completed'` is logged and no logged line contains
  `Ralph`).

## Verification

- `bun test` → **814 pass, 0 fail**, 1603 expect() calls, 29 files. Was 808 pass at the end of
  task #39; net **+6 tests**, all new coverage rather than pure renames.
- `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/task40-health-check` → succeeds
  (0.43 MB, 108 modules).
- Post-change `grep -ni ralph` over all 14 scoped files + run.ts: every surviving hit is either
  an intentional legacy fallback (category 1 for task #46) or owned by task #41/#48. Zero
  branding strings left in scope.

## Note on the harness's "BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED" banner

Root-caused it this iteration rather than just re-flagging it. `ralph.json`'s `healthCheck` is
already correct (`bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`), and
that command passes. The failure comes from the **frozen CLI binary**:
`~/.local/bin/ralph` is a symlink to `~/.local/bin/ralph-frozen`, pinned so the in-flight rename
cannot break the running loop. That binary predates the `--target=bun` fix in ralph.json and
still runs the old health-check string. This is the user's deliberate freeze, not a code defect —
it will clear itself when `./install.sh` is re-run after the rename round. No task filed
(tasks #34–#39 all flagged the same banner; this note supersedes those with the actual cause).

## Discovered tasks

None filed. The one cross-task gap found (the `/tmp/ralph-tts.pid` coupling) was attached as a
note to the existing task #48 rather than duplicated as a new task.

Create a new `migrate` command: src/commands/migrate.ts plus registration in src/index.ts. It converts one project from the .ralph/ layout to .cairn/.

BEHAVIOR (all settled decisions, do not re-litigate):

- `git mv` the data dir (.ralph -> .cairn) and the config file (ralph.json -> cairn.json). Verified behavior: git mv on a directory renames it on the filesystem AND stages the tracked renames, so untracked and gitignored files come along automatically — a single git mv handles everything inside.
- Rename the four stateful temp files inside the data dir: .ralph_completed_ids, .ralph_prev_notes, .ralph_iterations.log, .ralph_tasks_snapshot.json -> .cairn_* equivalents.
- Leave .ralph_task_*_notes.md and ALL archive files (tasks.completed.json, reviews/round-*.md, audit/) completely untouched — they are historical record and must move unmodified.
- Tolerate partial installs: one target project has no state.json, no reviews/ dir, and no installed agents. Nothing may assume a complete layout.
- STAGES CHANGES, NEVER COMMITS. The user reviews before it lands.

tasks.notes:
# Task #43 — `cairn migrate` command, core moves

## What was built

**`src/commands/migrate.ts`** (new) — exports `runMigrate(cwd: string, io?: MigrateIo): number`.
Returns a process exit code: `0` on success *and* on the already-migrated no-op, `1` on any refusal.
`MigrateIo` is an optional `{ log, warn, error }` injection point (defaults to `console.log` /
`console.error` / `console.error`) so the function is unit-testable without spawning.

**`src/index.ts`** — registers the `migrate` command. Two details worth keeping:
- The action calls `runMigrate(process.cwd())`, **not** `process.env.CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT`. That env var
  comes from `findProjectRoot()`, which walks upward; migrate must operate on the current directory
  only. There is a comment on the line saying so — don't "fix" it to use the project root.
- It sets `process.exitCode` rather than calling `process.exit()`, so Commander's async teardown runs.
- The import line now pulls `LEGACY` alongside `BRAND` from `./brand` (used in the description string).

## Behavior as implemented (order matters — every refusal happens before the first rename)

1. **Discovery, cwd only.** Checks `.cairn/`, `.ralph/`, `cairn.json`, `ralph.json` at `cwd`. If none of
   the four exist → error, exit 1. No upward walk, no scanning.
2. **Ambiguity refusals.** Both `.ralph/` and `.cairn/` present → refuse. Both `ralph.json` and
   `cairn.json` present → refuse. Migrate will not guess which one is live.
3. **Git repo required.** `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` must succeed. Rationale: the whole
   contract is "stages changes"; outside git there is nothing to stage. Clear error, exit 1.
4. **In-progress refusal.** Parses `<dataDir>/tasks.json` (plain `JSON.parse`, deliberately *not*
   `readTasksFile()` — that one repairs and can write, and preflight must have zero side effects).
   Any task with `status === 'in-progress'` → refuse, listing the ids. Unparseable tasks.json → also
   refuse (can't verify the invariant). Missing tasks.json → fine, skip the check.
5. **Dirty tree = warning only.** `git status --porcelain` non-empty → warn on stderr and continue.
6. **Moves**, via a `move()` helper that tries `git mv <rel> <rel>` and falls back to
   `fs.renameSync` when git refuses (untracked / gitignored path). Confirmed by the tests: the four
   stateful temp files are gitignored by the legacy `.gitignore`, so they all take the fallback path
   and print `(untracked — moved, nothing to stage)`.
   - `.ralph/` → `.cairn/` (one `git mv` carries untracked + gitignored contents along)
   - `ralph.json` → `cairn.json`
   - Then, inside the *new* data-dir path: `.ralph_completed_ids`, `.ralph_prev_notes`,
     `.ralph_iterations.log`, `.ralph_tasks_snapshot.json` → `.cairn_*`. If both names already
     exist for a suffix, it warns and leaves both (never clobbers live state).
7. **Untouched by design:** `.ralph_task_*_notes.md`, `tasks.completed.json`, `reviews/`, `audit/`.
   These come along inside the directory move, unmodified.
8. **Never commits.** Final output tells the user to review `git status` / `git diff --cached`.
9. **Idempotent.** A `moved === 0` run prints `Already on the .cairn/ layout — nothing to do.` and
   exits 0.
10. **Partial installs tolerated.** No `state.json`, no `reviews/`, no config file, no installed
    agents — nothing in the code assumes a complete layout.

## Tests

`test/commands/migrate.test.ts` — 12 tests, all passing. Per the task instruction they drive the real
entry point via `spawnSync('bun', ['run', src/index.ts, 'migrate'])` with `cwd` set to a temp git
fixture, **not** the installed binary (which is a frozen build for this round and has no `migrate`).

The `runCli` helper strips every `CAIRN_*` / `RALPH_*` var from the child env — otherwise the parent
loop's `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` leaks in and `setupProjectContext` resolves the wrong project.

`makeFixture()` builds a realistic legacy project: `git init`, tracked `tasks.json` /
`tasks.completed.json` / `planning-notes.md` / `state.json` / `reviews/round-1.md` /
`audit/findings.md` / `ralph.json`, a legacy `.gitignore` listing the `.ralph_*` names, the four
stateful temp files, and a `.ralph_task_7_notes.md` scratch file. Options: `statuses`, `partial`,
`alsoCairnDir`, `empty`, `commit`.

Coverage: command registration; dir + config rename; the four temp-file renames with content
preserved; scratch/archive files untouched; renames staged with commit count unchanged; partial
install; idempotency; in-progress refusal leaving everything in place; dirty-tree warning + proceed;
not-a-project error; both-dirs refusal; non-git-repo error.

## Verification

- `bun test` → **826 pass, 0 fail**, 30 files (was 814 before this task; +12).
- `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/task43-health` → succeeds, 0.43 MB, 109 modules.

The harness's "BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED / Browser build cannot import readline" banner is the same
stale-binary artifact noted in #40/#41/#42: `ralph.json` already carries `--target=bun`
(line 4), but the frozen `~/.local/bin/ralph` predates that config. Clears on `./install.sh` after
the rename round.

## Discovered task filed (1 of 3)

**#49 — migrate: refresh the data-dir .gitignore for `.cairn_*` temp names.** Real gap, deliberately
left out of #43's stated scope: the `.gitignore` *inside* the data dir moves over unmodified and
still lists only `.ralph_*` runtime names, so after migrating, every `.cairn_*` temp file a later run
writes shows up as untracked noise. Depends on #43.

## Note for #44 (`.claude` refresh and git staging)

`runMigrate` returns an exit code and takes an injectable `io` — extend it in place rather than
wrapping it. The `move()` helper already handles the tracked/untracked split; reuse it for any
further renames. The final "changes are STAGED, not committed" summary lines are at the bottom of the
function and should stay last.

Every subsequent run writes `.cairn_*` files, which are therefore NOT ignored and show up as untracked noise in git status.

Fix: in src/commands/migrate.ts, after the data-dir move, append any missing `.cairn_*` ignore lines to <dataDir>/.gitignore (keep the legacy lines — they are still read as a fallback). Match the two-block layout already used by GITIGNORE_CONTENT in src/commands/init.ts (current names, then a '# Legacy names' block). Must be idempotent: appending twice adds nothing. If .gitignore does not exist (partial install), do nothing. Stage the edit, never commit.

tasks.notes:
# Task #49 — migrate: refresh the data-dir .gitignore for `.cairn_*` temp names

## What changed

**`src/commands/init.ts`** — the ignore-name list is now data instead of a string blob, and it is
exported so migrate can reuse it (two hand-maintained lists would drift):

- `TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES` — the seven runtime temp names *minus* the prefix
  (`complete`, `iterations.log`, `prev_notes`, `task_meta`, `completed_ids`,
  `tasks_snapshot.json`, `task_*_notes.md`).
- `GITIGNORE_CURRENT_HEADER` / `GITIGNORE_LEGACY_HEADER` — the two block comments.
- `ignoreBlock(prefix)` — prefix + each suffix, one per line.
- `GITIGNORE_CONTENT` is now composed from those. **Byte-identical to the previous literal** —
  verified by the existing init tests, which still pass untouched.

**`src/commands/migrate.ts`** — new exported `refreshDataDirGitignore(dataDir): string[]`:

- Returns `[]` and does nothing if `<dataDir>/.gitignore` is absent (partial install).
- Reads the file, builds a `Set` of trimmed lines, and computes the missing `.cairn_*` names *and*
  the missing `.ralph_*` names.
- Appends `# Runtime temp files ...` + missing current names, then `# Legacy names ...` + missing
  legacy names — each block only if it has content. Existing lines are never rewritten or removed;
  legacy lines stay because they are still read as a fallback.
- Idempotent by construction (set membership on the whole file, not just the appended region), so a
  second run appends nothing. Also handles a file that doesn't end in a newline.

Call site in `runMigrate`, right after the temp-file renames and before the summary:

- Only when `dataDir` is non-null (config-only project ⇒ skipped).
- On a change: `git add <rel>` and log `added N ignore line(s) (staged)`; if `git add` fails
  (untracked/ignored .gitignore) it logs `(untracked)` instead. Never commits.
- The `moved === 0` "nothing to do" early return now also requires no gitignore change, so a project
  already on `.cairn/` with a stale ignore file gets fixed and reports
  `Refreshed .cairn/.gitignore in <cwd>.` instead of claiming there was nothing to do.

## Tests

`test/commands/migrate.test.ts` — new `migrate .gitignore refresh` describe, 7 tests, all driving the
real CLI via `bun run src/index.ts migrate` in a temp git fixture (same pattern as #43).

Fixture gained a `gitignore?: string | null` option (`undefined` = the legacy default,
`null` = write no `.gitignore` at all, string = custom content).

Coverage: all seven `.cairn_*` names appended while legacy lines and `instructions.md` survive;
byte-identical second run; no duplicate when some `.cairn_*` lines already exist; both blocks
appended (current before legacy, with the `# Legacy names` header) when the file has no legacy lines;
no `.gitignore` created when the data dir has none; the appended lines land **in the index**
(asserted via `git show :.cairn/.gitignore`) with the commit count unchanged; the idempotent second
run still prints `nothing to do`.

## Verification

- `bun test test/commands/migrate.test.ts` → 19 pass, 0 fail (was 12).
- `bun test` → **833 pass, 0 fail**, 30 files (was 826; +7).
- `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/task49-health` → succeeds, 0.43 MB, 109 modules.

The harness's "BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED / Browser build cannot import readline" banner is the same
stale-binary artifact seen in #40–#43: `ralph.json:4` already carries `--target=bun`, but the frozen
`~/.local/bin/ralph` predates it. Clears on `./install.sh`.

## Notes for later tasks

- `migrate.ts` now imports from `init.ts`. That is a one-way dependency (init does not import
  migrate) and pulls in nothing new — init has no readline import. If init ever grows a readline
  import at module scope, migrate's browser-target build would break; keep the prompt plumbing in
  `src/index.ts`.
- Anything that adds a new runtime temp file should add its suffix to `TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES` — that
  single edit updates both `cairn init` and `cairn migrate`.
- No discovered tasks filed this iteration.

tasks.description:
Extend the migrate command from task 43 to refresh installed artifacts and stage everything it touched.

1. Re-install agents and slash commands by reusing installAgents() and installSlashCommands() from src/commands/init.ts — they already overwrite via copyFileSync. Install the FULL current set even where none existed previously: one target project has zero installed agents and this is its upgrade path.
2. NON-DESTRUCTIVE RULE: overwrite by filename only. Never delete, never sync-and-prune, never touch files outside the source set. One target project has a custom .claude/agents/frontend-code-analyzer.md that must survive untouched.
3. Regenerate the three .claude/hooks/*.sh scripts for the new socket path — but ONLY if hooks already exist in that project. Do not create hooks where there were none.
4. Rewrite the data dir's .gitignore with both .cairn_* and .ralph_* prefixes, PRESERVING any custom lines the project added (one project appended 'instructions.md').
5. GIT STAGING: git mv stages itself, but everything else here does not. Explicitly `git add` all non-git-mv output — the rewritten .gitignore, regenerated hooks, and any newly installed agent/command files. Without this they sit unstaged, or for a project that never had them, entirely UNTRACKED — so the user would review an incomplete `git diff --cached` and think the migration was smaller than it was.
6. Finish by printing a `git status` style summary of exactly what was staged.

Must remain idempotent. TDD via temp git fixture using `bun run src/index.ts migrate`, not the installed binary.
tasks.notes:
# Task #44 — migrate: .claude refresh and git staging

## What changed

**`src/commands/init.ts`** — the three installers are now reusable and report what they did:

- `installSlashCommands(projectRoot, cairnRoot?, opts?)` and `installAgents(...)` now **return
  `string[]`** of project-relative paths actually written, and share one private `installMdDir()`
  (the two were byte-for-byte the same loop). Signatures are backwards compatible — existing init
  callers/tests are untouched.
- New `InstallOptions { skipUnchanged?, log? }`. `skipUnchanged` leaves byte-identical destinations
  alone and omits them from the result; `log` redirects the per-file line (default `console.log`, so
  init's output is unchanged). `skipUnchanged` is what makes migrate idempotent — see below.
- New exported `NARRATION_HOOKS` (`{name, event, content}` × narrate/speak/notify) and
  `writeNarrationHooks(projectRoot, opts?)`, which writes + chmods 755 and returns the paths.
  `installNarrationHooks()` (the interactive init path) now delegates to it and emits the exact same
  `  Created: .claude/hooks/x.sh (Event)` lines in the same order.

**`src/commands/migrate.ts`**:

- New exported `refreshClaudeArtifacts(cwd): string[]` — reinstalls the FULL current command + agent
  set (even where `.claude/` did not exist: that is the upgrade path for a project that never ran
  init), then regenerates the three hooks **only if at least one of them already exists**. Overwrite
  by filename only; nothing is deleted, nothing outside the source set is read. A project's own
  `.claude/agents/frontend-code-analyzer.md` and `.claude/commands/*.md` survive untouched.
- Staging: `git mv` stages itself, but the gitignore rewrite and every installed artifact do not, so
  each installed path gets an explicit `git add -- <rel>`. If the add fails (path ignored by git) it
  warns and keeps going instead of aborting.
- New closing summary. `record(label, detail)` accumulates `git status`-style lines
  (`  renamed:   .ralph -> .cairn`, `  new file:  .claude/agents/planner.md`) printed under a
  `Staged changes:` header before the final "Changes are STAGED, not committed" line. Labels for
  installed files come from git itself — after the add, `git diff --cached --name-status -M -- <rel>`
  is parsed (A/M/R/C/D/T → `STATUS_LABELS`) rather than guessing new-vs-modified. Empty output means
  the write matched HEAD, so the file is silently dropped from the summary.
- The "nothing to do" early return now also requires `installed.length === 0`, and the moved === 0
  message became `Refreshed Cairn artifacts in <cwd>.` (was `.gitignore`-specific).

**`src/index.ts`** — migrate's `--help` description now mentions the artifact refresh.

## Idempotency

Comes from `skipUnchanged`, not from a second layer of bookkeeping: run two re-copies nothing, so
`installed` is empty, nothing is staged, and the run prints "nothing to do". Deliberately NOT based
on `git diff --cached` for those paths — run one leaves them staged-but-uncommitted, so git would
still report them on run two and the no-op run would look like it did work.

## Tests

`test/commands/migrate.test.ts` — new `migrate .claude refresh` describe, 8 tests, all through the
real CLI (`bun run src/index.ts migrate`) in a temp git fixture. Fixture gained a
`claude?: Record<string, string>` option (paths relative to `.claude/`).

Covered: full agent+command set installed into a project with no `.claude/` (content compared against
the repo's `agents/`+`commands/`, read dynamically so the list can't drift); every new file staged
(asserted via `git show :.claude/agents/planner.md`, i.e. really in the index) with the commit count
unchanged; stale `planner.md` overwritten while a custom `frontend-code-analyzer.md` and a custom
`commands/deploy.md` survive and stay out of the diff; all three hooks regenerated on the
`/tmp/cairn-tts.sock` path + exec bit + staged when only `narrate.sh` pre-existed; NO hooks dir
created where there were none; second run stages nothing new and says "nothing to do"; the
`Staged changes:` summary shows renamed/modified/new file lines; and a project already on `.cairn/`
with a tampered agent gets refreshed instead of reporting "nothing to do".

TDD confirmed: with `src/commands/{migrate,init}.ts` stashed, 6 of the 8 new tests fail (the two
negative ones — no-hooks-created and idempotency — pass vacuously, as expected).

## Verification

- `bun test test/commands/migrate.test.ts` → 27 pass, 0 fail (was 19).
- `bun test` → **841 pass, 0 fail**, 30 files (was 833; +8).
- `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/task44-health` → 0.44 MB, 109 modules.
- Manual smoke run on a scratch repo with a legacy layout, a custom agent, and one legacy-socket
  hook: 3 paths moved, 13 ignore lines added, 7 artifacts installed, `narrate.sh` modified +
  `speak.sh`/`notify.sh` created, summary printed, custom agent intact, second run "nothing to do".

The harness's "BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED / Browser build cannot import readline" banner is the same
stale-binary artifact as #40–#43/#49: `ralph.json:4` already carries `--target=bun`; the frozen
`~/.local/bin/ralph` predates it. Clears on `./install.sh`.

## Notes for later tasks

- `migrate.ts` → `init.ts` is still a one-way import. `writeNarrationHooks` and `installMdDir` keep
  all readline/prompt plumbing out of that path, so migrate's browser-target build stays clean.
- Anything new under `.claude/` that init installs should be added to `refreshClaudeArtifacts()` too,
  or migrated projects will keep a stale copy forever.
- Not filed as a task, but worth knowing: `installAgents`/`installSlashCommands` silently no-op when
  `resolveCairnRoot()` can't find the repo's `agents/`/`commands/` dirs (pre-existing init behavior,
  now also reachable from migrate).
- No discovered tasks filed this iteration.

`src/commands/run.ts`, `src/commands/narrate.ts`, `.claude/hooks/*.sh`) and found:

Every one is now accounted for:

| Bucket | Lines | Where |
|---|---|---|

- `resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain` lost the `env.RALPH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` leg; the chain is now `CAIRN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. `AnthropicApiKeyResolution['source']` is now `'cairn' | 'plain' | 'none'`.
- `warnIfLegacyApiKey` deleted entirely.
- Imports narrowed from `{ BRAND, LEGACY, warnLegacyOnce }` to `{ BRAND }` — both `LEGACY` and `warnLegacyOnce` became unused here. They are still used elsewhere in `src/` (utils, narration, run, init), so `src/brand.ts` is untouched.
- The resolved key is still **not** normalized onto plain `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; the doc comment explaining why (the loop blanks that name to force Max-plan usage) is preserved verbatim minus the legacy sentence.

**src/commands/narrate.ts** and **src/commands/run.ts** — deleted the `warnIfLegacyApiKey(resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain())` statement and the whole `import … from '../config'` line in each. In both files those were the only symbols imported from `../config`, so the import lines went entirely rather than being narrowed.

## Test changes (TDD — 3 red, then green)

**test/config.test.ts**
- Dropped `warnIfLegacyApiKey` from the import list and removed the now-unused `resetLegacyWarnings` import from `../src/brand`.
- Rewrote `loadConfig — dual-read config file discovery` as `loadConfig — config file discovery`: kept the cairn.json / no-config cases, replaced the fallback case with `ignores a ralph.json left behind by an unmigrated project`, and replaced the warn-once case with `emits no warnings when loading config`.
- `findConfigFile` describe: the legacy-resolution test became `resolves to cairn.json even when only a ralph.json exists`. All assertions are literal `'cairn.json'`, never `BRAND.configFile`.
- `resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain` describe: dropped the legacy leg tests, added `ignores a RALPH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY still exported by an old shell profile` (expects `{key: undefined, source: 'none'}`), and kept the never-normalize guard (now keyed off `CAIRN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).
- Deleted the whole `warnIfLegacyApiKey` describe.
- Mechanical: every fixture that wrote `ralph.json` and expected it to load (the `loadConfig` and `loadConfig review.postTask` blocks) now writes `cairn.json`; test title `sets all RALPH_* env vars` → `sets all CAIRN_* env vars` (it always asserted CAIRN_ names).

**test/commands/narrate.test.ts** — no change needed. It never referenced `warnIfLegacyApiKey`, the API key chain, or `ralph.json`. Its only `ralph` mention is `expect(output).not.toContain('/tmp/ralph-tts')` at line 236, which belongs to the socket tier (task #52). Confirmed green as-is (16 pass).

## Out-of-scope files I had to touch, and why

Two test files outside the task's file list broke as direct fallout. Both were fixed:

1. **test/commands/edit.test.ts** — this one is worth knowing about: the test `target "config" resolves an existing legacy ralph.json` wrote only a `ralph.json`, so once `findConfigFile` stopped resolving it, `runEdit` hit its not-found path and called the **real** `process.exit(1)`. That killed the bun test *runner process* mid-suite: `bun test` exited 1 after 8 files with no summary line and no failure attributed to edit.test.ts (running that file alone printed only the version banner). If a future removal task sees `bun test` end abruptly with no summary, look for a test that reaches an unmocked `process.exit`. ## What changed

  `.claude/hooks/narrate.sh` + `HOOK_SOCKET_RE` probe as step 1 (deliberate, per the task:
  the hooks are the socket's only clients, so whatever they dial wins). The two-candidate
  `/tmp` loop over `[BRAND.socket, LEGACY.socket]` is gone; with no hook match it now just
  returns `BRAND.socket`.
- `findNarrationPidFile(deps?)` — keeps its signature, body is now `return BRAND.pidFile`.

  *why the hook file is authoritative* explanation is kept (including the "silently dead —
  server up, hooks fire, events go nowhere" point).

## The one judgment call: the PathProbeDeps seam

The task says to KEEP the `PathProbeDeps` injection seam. With a single candidate per path,
an existence check can no longer change the answer — `exists(BRAND.socket) ? BRAND.socket :
BRAND.socket` is dead code — so I did **not** write a vestigial check. Instead:

- `PathProbeDeps` stays exported and stays on both signatures (params renamed to `_deps`).
- Its doc comment now says explicitly that both resolvers currently ignore it, and why it
  stays: these are the resolution entry points, and a future candidate would need it back.

Consequence for future editors: **tests may still pass `{exists: ...}` to these two functions,
but it has no effect.** The retained tests that pass a probe (`NONE`, `{exists: () => true}`)
are asserting "the answer is BRAND.* regardless of what is live in /tmp", which is exactly
the post-removal contract — but do not add a new test that expects an injected `exists` to
steer the result; it won't.

The `RunRunDeps.findNarrationSocketPath` seam in `src/commands/run.ts` is untouched and still
works — that is a different seam (run.ts injects the whole resolver function), and
`test/commands/run.test.ts:1434` still pins it.

    socket when it is already live`.

  - `warns once when it resolves to the legacy socket` deleted; `does not warn when...` →

    `console.error` output).
- `findNarrationPidFile` describe: legacy-fallback test → **`ignores a stale /tmp/ralph-tts.pid
  left by the pre-rename binary`** (← red #2), plus a new `emits no warnings when a stale legacy

  constant when `LEGACY` is deleted.

  `task_<id>_notes.md`" rather than spelling the prefix out — writing `.ralph_task_...`
  in a comment inside `src/**/*.ts` would itself trip legacy-markers (it matches
  `/ralph/i` on any line, comments included). **Keep it phrased that way until #62/#63.**

line 72). Rather than leave a dead legacy export in `init.ts`, I moved the constant into

starts from a pre-rename project and still needs one.

# Task #58 — src/utils.ts: collapse data-dir tier, delete temp-file resolvers

## Outcome

All 7 `remove once all projects migrated` markers in `src/utils.ts` are gone; the
file no longer imports `LEGACY` or `warnLegacyOnce` (only `BRAND`).

Pre-delete verification, as the task required:
`grep -rn "findTempFilePath\|allTempFilePaths" src/ test/` → only `src/utils.ts`
and `test/utils.test.ts`. Tasks 55/56 had indeed migrated all five external
callers, so deletion was safe. Post-change sweep for all four deleted symbols →
no stale references anywhere.

TDD: wrote/rewrote the tests first as **positive assertions that the legacy tier is
gone** (rather than only deleting tests, which can never go red), ran them against
the still-dual-reading source → **4 fail**, then made the source change → green.

- `bun test test/utils.test.ts test/index.test.ts` → **50 pass, 0 fail**
- `bun test` → **838 pass, 0 fail, 31 files** (down from #57's 849 — exactly the
  11 net tests removed, see accounting below; no regressions)
- `test/legacy-markers.test.ts` → passes within the full run
- Health check `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`
  → OK. Did **not** touch `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck`; did **not** run `./install.sh`.

## src/utils.ts

- **Deleted** `dataDirNameAt` and `warnIfLegacyDataDir` outright.
- **`findDataDir(projectRoot)`** keeps its name and signature but collapses to a
  one-liner: `return join(projectRoot, BRAND.dataDir)`. Note the task text said
  "plain existence check" — with only one candidate left, *both* branches of that
  check return the identical path, so the check is provably dead code. The
  one-liner is behaviorally identical to an existence-checking version. Callers
  still route through this helper, so the standing "never build data paths from
  `BRAND.dataDir` directly" rule still has a single enforcement point.
- **`findProjectRoot`** — the upward walk now does
  `statSync(join(dir, BRAND.dataDir)).isDirectory()` inline at each level.
  **The `isDirectory()` semantics are deliberately preserved**: a plain
  `existsSync` would make a stray `.cairn` *file* stop the walk at the wrong
  directory. `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT` stays priority #1; git-root and cwd fallbacks
  unchanged; legacy note dropped from the doc comment.
- **Deleted** `findTempFilePath` and `allTempFilePaths` entirely. `tempFilePath`
  and the `── Runtime temp files ──` banner stay, minus the dual-read framing.
- `statSync` import retained (now used by `findProjectRoot`); `existsSync`
  retained (used by `resolveCairnRoot`).

## test/utils.test.ts

- Dropped `findTempFilePath`/`allTempFilePaths` from the import line, and the
  `resetLegacyWarnings` import (no utils code path emits legacy warnings now).
- **First `findProjectRoot` describe**: renamed the `.ralph` fixtures to `.cairn`.
  These were *not* cosmetic — they are behavioral assertions that would have gone
  red once the legacy leg was removed, so they had to move in this task even
  though task 64 owns the cosmetic fixture sweep. Task 64 will find them done.
- Deleted the whole `findProjectRoot — dual-read data directory discovery`
  describe (7 tests). Two of its tests were duplicates of the renamed ones above;
  the coverage worth keeping was rehomed into the first describe as:
  - `ignores a .cairn entry that is not a directory` (guards the `isDirectory()`
    semantics; restructured as parent-`.cairn`-dir / child-`.cairn`-file so it
    actually discriminates instead of passing via the cwd fallback)
  - `does not treat a legacy .ralph/ directory as a project root` (nearest-wins
    case, inverted — this was one of the 4 red tests)
- `findDataDir` describe: deleted the two legacy tests, added
  `never resolves to a legacy .ralph directory` (red before the change).
  Dropped the now-pointless `console.error` stubbing / `resetLegacyWarnings`.
- `runtime temp file paths` → renamed to `tempFilePath` with 2 tests; the
  `findTempFilePath` (4) and `allTempFilePaths` (1) blocks are gone.

## test/index.test.ts

- Deleted `falls back to an existing legacy .ralph/ data dir`, replaced with
  `never resolves to a leftover .ralph/ directory` (same fixture, inverted
  expectation — red before the change).
- `points completedTasksPath at a legacy .ralph/ data dir` → rewritten as
  `points completedTasksPath at .cairn/ even when a leftover .ralph/ exists`.
- **Scope note (beyond the two tests named in the task):** also deleted
  `prefers .cairn/ when both layouts exist`. It still passed, but "both layouts"
  is no longer a concept that exists — the test asserted a *preference* between
  two candidates where only one candidate remains. Renamed
  `defaults to .cairn/ when neither layout exists` →
  `...when the data dir does not exist yet` for the same reason.

Test-count accounting for 849 → 838: utils.test.ts −10 (−7 dual-read describe,
+2 rehomed; −2 findDataDir legacy, +1 inverted; −5 temp-file, +2 tempFilePath),
index.test.ts −1 (−2 deleted, +1 inverted).

## Notes for future tasks

- **Task 63 (`src/brand.ts` — delete LEGACY):** `LEGACY.tempPrefix` now has zero
  readers in `src/` — `src/utils.ts` was its last consumer. `LEGACY.dataDir` is
  still referenced by `src/commands/migrate.ts` and by `src/index.ts:189`
  (migrate's help text), both of which task 60 deletes. So 60 should land before 63.
- **Task 64 (cosmetic fixture sweep):** `test/utils.test.ts` and the data-dir
  portion of `test/index.test.ts` are already clean of `.ralph` fixtures; the only
  remaining `.ralph` strings there are in the two intentional *negative* tests
  (`never resolves to a legacy .ralph directory`, `never resolves to a leftover
  .ralph/ directory`), which must keep the literal to mean anything. Do not
  "clean" those.
- No discovered tasks this iteration — the task matched the codebase exactly.

# Task #63 — src/brand.ts: delete LEGACY, rehome the permanent notes prefix

## Outcome

`src/brand.ts` now exports exactly two things: `BRAND` and the new
`NOTES_TEMP_PREFIX`. `LEGACY`, `warnLegacyOnce`, `resetLegacyWarnings`, and the
module-level `warnedKeys` set are gone. Full suite: **805 pass, 0 fail, 29
files** (was 806 — net −1: removed 4 LEGACY/warnLegacyOnce tests, added 3).
Health check (`bun build --target=bun`) bundles clean.

## Pre-delete verification

`grep -rn "LEGACY\|warnLegacyOnce\|resetLegacyWarnings" src/ test/` before
touching anything found exactly what the task predicted — no surviving callers
of the two functions anywhere, and only three `LEGACY` consumers left, all of
them the `tempPrefix` field:

- `src/commands/run.ts:51` (buildSystemPrompt's `notesFile`)
- `src/commands/run.ts:366` (`NOTES_TEMPFILE_RE`)
- `src/commands/init.ts:41` (the `.gitignore` block)

All three now read `NOTES_TEMP_PREFIX`. After the change, the only match in the
whole tree is the guard assertion in `test/brand.test.ts` itself.

`grep -rn "remove once all projects migrated" src/ lib/ install.sh` now returns
**zero hits** — the three that task #62 catalogued (brand.ts:32, run.ts:363,
run.ts:708) were all in this task's scope and are all gone. The removal round's
work list is empty.

## The new constant

```ts
export const NOTES_TEMP_PREFIX = '.ralph_';
```

Doc comment states plainly that it is a PERMANENT exception and NOT a
compatibility fallback — nothing resolves against `BRAND.tempPrefix` as an
alternative. Rationale recorded inline: write-and-sweep scratch never read
back, so the name only has to be agreed on by writer and sweeper, and renaming
would churn committed `.gitignore` history for zero behavioural gain.

The `BRAND` doc comment keeps the CREATE-vs-RESOLVE standing rule verbatim;
only its closing clause changed, from "a project still on the legacy layout
gets paths pointing at something that does not exist" to a
legacy-framing-free statement of the same failure mode.

## Deviation from the task description — read this if you touch the sweep

The description suggested `NOTES_TEMPFILE_RE` "can now match NOTES_TEMP_PREFIX
alone, since `.cairn_task_*_notes.md` was never written." **I kept the
two-branch alternation**, reordered to `[NOTES_TEMP_PREFIX, BRAND.tempPrefix]`.

Reason: `test/commands/run.test.ts:2031/2051` already asserts that
`.cairn_task_7_notes.md` IS swept, with the comment "The sweep must cover the
current-brand prefix too, or new scratch files linger forever." Narrowing the
regex would have meant deleting a passing test and its stated rationale in
order to make the sweep strictly less robust against an agent that spells the
scratch file with the current prefix. The task's own hard requirement — "the
sweep must keep matching this prefix or scratch leaks forever" — is about
`.ralph_`, and that branch is intact and now first in the alternation. Both
prefixes are covered by the init.ts `.gitignore` block either way
(`TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES` includes `task_*_notes.md` under `BRAND.tempPrefix`),
so nothing is left untracked.

The comment above the regex now says which branch is load-bearing
(`NOTES_TEMP_PREFIX` — the prompt hands it out) and which is defensive
(`BRAND.tempPrefix`), so the distinction survives the next reader.

## Stale comments fixed

- run.ts ~364 (`NOTES_TEMPFILE_RE`): dropped "the alternation collapses to
  BRAND only" — that was written when the notes file was expected to be
  renamed. It never will be, so the claim was actively misleading.

tasks.title: Health check runs from the task directory, so root-relative healthCheck commands fail spuriously
tasks.description: src/health-check.ts:55 computes `cwd = taskDir ? join(projectRoot, taskDir) : projectRoot` and runs the project-level `healthCheck` command there. But `healthCheck` is a single project-wide string in cairn.json, written relative to the project root — cairn's own is `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`. For any task whose `directory` field is not the project root, that command is executed from `<root>/<directory>` and fails on paths that resolve fine from the root. Observed live in iteration 16: task #66 has `directory: "src"`, so the pre-iteration health check ran from `<root>/src`, where `src/index.ts` does not exist, and the agent was handed a `BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED: FileNotFound opening root directory "src"` banner describing a build that is actually green (verified: the same command from the project root succeeds). This is a false failure signal on every non-root task and wastes agent attention chasing a nonexistent break. Decide and implement one of: (a) always run `healthCheck` from `projectRoot` and drop the `taskDir` join — simplest, matches the fact that the command is project-wide; (b) keep the per-directory cwd but make it opt-in via a per-directory health check config. Prefer (a) unless there is a known consumer relying on per-directory cwd. Note that `shouldRunHealthCheck()` also probes `join(cwd, 'package.json')` for the `npm run type-check` special case and has the same cwd assumption — fix both together. Update test/health-check.test.ts to cover a non-root taskDir with a root-relative command.
tasks.notes:
# Task #68 — health check and test validator ran from the task directory

Fixed in iteration 18 alongside #66. Chose **option (a)** from the task description: both the
project-wide health check and the task's `tests` commands now always run from `projectRoot`.

## Why (a), not (b)

`healthCheck` is a single project-wide string in `cairn.json`, and task `tests` entries are
likewise written relative to the project root (#66's are `bun test test/config.test.ts` and
`bun test`). There is no per-directory variant of either, so there was never a consumer relying
on per-directory cwd — the join was simply wrong. Option (b) would have added config surface to
preserve a behavior nothing wanted.

## Changes

- **`src/health-check.ts`** — `cwd` is now `projectRoot` unconditionally. **`taskDir` was removed
  from `HealthCheckOpts` entirely**, not just ignored: with no field to pass, the bug becomes
  unrepresentable at the type level, which is a stronger guarantee than any test. This also fixes
  `shouldRunHealthCheck()`, which probed `join(cwd, 'package.json')` and so silently skipped the
  `npm run type-check` special case for every non-root task.
- **`src/commands/run.ts`** — dropped `taskDir` from the `runHealthCheck` deps signature (line
  ~279) and from the call site (line ~529). `taskDir` is still used elsewhere in the loop for
  `mkdirSync(taskDirAbs)` and as the agent's spawn cwd — those are correct and untouched.
- **`src/test-validator.ts`** — `cwd` is now `path.resolve(projectRoot)`; the
  `task.directory && task.directory !== '/'` derivation is gone. Comment records why.
- **`test/health-check.test.ts`** — dropped `taskDir` from all call sites; `taskDir resolution`
  describe → `cwd resolution`, covering: runs in projectRoot; a root-relative command referencing
  `sub/index.ts` succeeds; the type-check guard probes `projectRoot/package.json`.
- **`test/test-validator.test.ts`** — `directory resolution` describe → `cwd resolution`. The test
  that asserted `task.directory` was honored is inverted into a regression test: a task with
  `directory: 'sub'` and a root-relative test command now **passes** and stays `complete`; a
  command relative to `sub/` now **fails**.

## TDD

Wrote the tests first. Red run: 2 failures in `test-validator` (root-relative command from a
subdir task returned `failed`; subdir-relative command returned `passed`). The health-check tests
passed pre-fix only because omitting `taskDir` already fell through to `projectRoot` — the real
change there is the type-level removal of the field. After the fix: `bun test` → **799 pass,
0 fail, 29 files**; `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck` clean.

## Impact

This was the cause of two false signals that had been wasting iterations:

1. The cosmetic `BUILD HEALTH CHECK FAILED: FileNotFound opening root directory "src"` banner
   handed to every agent working a non-root task.
2. The far more damaging one — `validateTaskTests()` misclassifying the resulting failure as real
   and reverting the task to in-progress. This reverted task #66 in iterations 16 and 17, and
   since #66 (priority 16) outranks #68 (priority 20), the loop re-selected #66 forever.

**The running `cairn run` process loaded the old code at startup**, so it will still revert #66
once more at the end of iteration 18. Stop the run, `./install.sh` (or `bun run build`), restart.
Per CLAUDE.md's pin/unpin procedure, iteration 18 did not run `./install.sh` itself and did not
modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck`.

tasks.description: Task #51 deleted warnIfLegacyApiKey and its two call sites (src/commands/narrate.ts, src/commands/run.ts), which were the only consumers of resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain(). The function is still exported from src/config.ts and covered by test/config.test.ts, but nothing in src/ calls it — the resolution is now purely documentary, mirroring the same chain in lib/cairn_narrate_server.py (see task #59). Either (a) delete the helper, its AnthropicApiKeyResolution type, and its tests, leaving the Python server as the single implementation, or (b) keep it and give it a real caller — e.g. have runNarrate/runRun pass the resolved key into the narration server env instead of relying on the child process re-reading the environment. Do NOT normalize onto plain ANTHROPIC_API_KEY under either option: the loop deliberately blanks that name to force Max-plan usage. Sequence this after #59 so both sides of the mirror are decided together.

## Decision (made in iteration 16): option (a) — deleted the helper

Recorded here so nobody re-litigates it:

1. **Option (b) would have had no behavioral effect.** Its premise was "pass the resolved key
   into the narration server env instead of relying on the child re-reading the environment."
   But `startNarrationServer()` (`src/narration.ts`) spawns the Python server with
   `{ detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' }` and **no `env` option**, so the child inherits the
   parent's `process.env` verbatim. The `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` blanking is *per-spawn and
   non-mutating* — every site builds a fresh object (`{ ...process.env, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: '' }`
   in `run.ts`, `plan.ts`, `summarize.ts`, `post-task-reviewer.ts`); the parent's own
   `process.env` is never touched. The narration server already sees the real key under
   whichever name the user exported.
2. **Option (b) could not have collapsed the mirror either.** `lib/cairn_narrate_server.py` is a
   standalone `argparse` script that can be launched directly, so it must keep its own
   resolution chain regardless. (b) would have left two implementations *plus* new env
   plumbing; (a) leaves exactly one, sited where the key is actually consumed.

Changes (all in 706e1a3): `src/config.ts` lost the `AnthropicApiKeyResolution` interface and
`resolveAnthropicApiKeyChain()`; `test/config.test.ts` lost the 6-test describe block (805 → 799);
`lib/cairn_narrate_server.py` (~line 224) absorbed the load-bearing "never normalize the resolved
value back onto plain `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`" invariant that had lived only in the deleted TS
docstring. `src/commands/narrate.ts` and `src/commands/run.ts` needed no change — task #51 had
already removed `warnIfLegacyApiKey` and both call sites.

## Why this task kept reverting — and what iteration 18 did about it

#66 was marked complete in iterations 16 and 17 and **reverted both times by cairn's own
post-iteration validator**. The revert was a false negative, diagnosed in iteration 17 and
**fixed in iteration 18** (see `.ralph_task_68_notes.md`): `src/test-validator.ts` ran the task's
root-relative `tests` entries from `<root>/<task.directory>`, i.e. `<root>/src`, where
`bun test test/config.test.ts` matches nothing. Bun's stderr for a non-matching filter matches
none of `CANT_RUN_PATTERNS`, so `isCantRunError()` returned false and it was classified as a real
failure → task reverted to in-progress.

Because #66 (priority 16) outranks #68 (priority 20), the loop re-selected #66 every iteration —
a livelock. #66 needed zero code work, so iteration 18 spent itself fixing #68, the sole blocker
and the only other remaining task. That is a deliberate departure from one-task-per-iteration,
taken because doing only #66 was provably a no-op for the third time running.

at startup**, so its post-iteration validator is still the buggy one. Expect #66 to be reverted to
in-progress one final time at the end of iteration 18. That revert is spurious — the code is done.

To pick up the fix: stop the run, `./install.sh` (or `bun run build`), and restart. Per CLAUDE.md's
pin/unpin procedure this iteration did **not** run `./install.sh` and did **not** touch
`cairn.json`'s `healthCheck`.

tasks.description:
`src/test-validator.ts:19` defines CANT_RUN_PATTERNS = ['missing script', 'not found', 'no such file', 'enoent', 'cannot find module', 'module not found'], and isCantRunError(stderr, exitCode) at :57 returns true only on exit 127 or a case-insensitive substring hit. This classifier is the SOLE gate between 'infrastructure problem — note it' and 'real test failure — revert the task to in-progress' (:118-124).

It has a hole that cost three iterations last round. Measured from <root>/src: `bun test test/config.test.ts` exits 1 with `Tests need ".test", "_test_"...` (filter matched nothing), and `bun build --compile src/index.ts` exits 1 with `FileNotFound opening root directory "src"`. Neither matches any pattern — note `filenotfound` has NO SPACE, so the existing 'not found' entry misses it. A completed task was therefore reverted to in-progress, and because selectNextTask (`src/task-selector.ts:48`) returns any in-progress task ahead of all pending work, the loop re-picked it every iteration until a human intervened.

Broaden the classifier:
(1) Add `filenotfound` and `file not found` to CANT_RUN_PATTERNS.
(2) Add bun's non-matching-filter signal. VERIFY the exact current wording yourself by running `bun test test/does-not-exist.test.ts` from the project root and matching a stable fragment of what it actually prints — do not guess the string.
(3) Add a ZERO-TESTS-RAN check: if the output indicates no tests were collected or executed, classify as can't-run regardless of exit code. A command that ran no tests is never evidence of a real failure.

IMPORTANT: runCommand (:28-55) currently captures ONLY stderr. If bun writes the relevant line to stdout, the classifier cannot see it — in that case widen runCommand to capture both streams and feed both to the classifier, rather than silently missing the signal. Keep the existing case-insensitive matching.

# Task #69 — Broaden isCantRunError so a command that ran no tests is never a real failure

## What changed

`src/test-validator.ts`:

1. **New CANT_RUN_PATTERNS entries** — `filenotfound`, `file not found`, `did not match any test files`.
2. **New ZERO_TESTS_PATTERNS** (regex list, checked in `isCantRunError` after the substring
   patterns, regardless of exit code):
   - `/\bran\s+0\s+tests?\b/` — bun's `Ran 0 tests across 1 file.`
   - `/\b0\s+tests?\s+(ran|found|executed|collected)\b/`
   - `/\bno\s+tests?\s+(ran|found|were\s+found|to\s+run|were\s+run|executed|collected)\b/`
   - `/\bno\s+test\s+files?\s+found\b/`
   Regexes rather than substrings so `0 tests` can't match inside e.g. `430 tests`.
3. **`runCommand` now captures stdout as well as stderr**, returning `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr }`.
   The call site builds `output = stdout + "\n" + stderr` and feeds that to `isCantRunError`.
   The failure message also uses `output.trim().slice(-200)` instead of stderr-only, so a
   stdout-only runner no longer produces an empty message.
   Timeout detection still keys off the dedicated `stderr` sentinel (`timeout after Nms`),
   unchanged.

Matching stays case-insensitive (`output.toLowerCase()` before both checks).

## VERIFIED strings (bun 1.3.11, af24e281) — measured, not guessed

Both signals go to **stderr**; only the `bun test v...` banner goes to stdout.

- `bun test test/does-not-exist.test.ts` (exit 1), stderr:
  ```
  The following filters did not match any test files in --cwd="/Users/jhummel/Documents/_Repos/cairn":
   test/does-not-exist.test.ts
  95 files were searched [4.00ms]

  note: Tests need ".test", "_test_", ".spec" or "_spec_" in the filename (ex: "MyApp.test.ts")
  ```
  Stable fragment chosen: `did not match any test files`. (Deliberately NOT the
  `Tests need ".test"...` note — that line is quote-heavy and more likely to be reworded.)
- `bun build --compile src/index.ts` from `<root>/src` (exit 1), stderr:
  `FileNotFound opening root directory "src"` — one word, which is exactly why the
  pre-existing `not found` entry missed it.
- Zero-test suite (exit 0), stderr: `Ran 0 tests across 1 file. [7.00ms]`.

Since bun uses stderr for all of these, the stdout capture was not strictly required for
bun. It was added anyway per the task's IMPORTANT clause because other runners (pytest,
vitest, go test) report the same conditions on stdout, and a signal the classifier cannot
see is a signal that destroys finished work. There is one test covering this path
explicitly (`classifies a can't-run signal written to stdout, not just stderr`).

## Tests

`test/test-validator.test.ts`, 5 new cases in the existing `infrastructure errors (cant run)`
describe block. Each asserts `status === 'error'` AND that the task in tasks.json is still
`complete` with `completedAt`/`completedBy` intact (i.e. NOT reverted to in-progress):

- bun build `FileNotFound` (no space)
- spaced `file not found`
- bun filter-no-match wording
- `Ran 0 tests across 1 file.` with exit 1
- can't-run signal on stdout only

TDD confirmed: 4 of the 5 failed before the implementation (`Expected: "error", Received:
"failed"`). The spaced `file not found` case passed immediately because `not found` is
already a substring of it — kept as a regression guard for that pattern.

## Verification

- `bun test test/test-validator.test.ts` → 27 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test` (full suite) → **804 pass, 0 fail**, 29 files.
- Health check `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck-task69` → clean.
- **End-to-end reproduction of the round-losing scenario**: called `validateTaskTests` with
  `projectRoot: <root>/src` and the two real commands from the task description
  (`bun test test/config.test.ts`, `bun build --compile src/index.ts ...`). Both now return
  `status: 'error'` and leave the task at `complete`. Before this change both returned
  `'failed'` and reverted it.

## Notes for the next agent

- This is a defense-in-depth layer, independent of the cwd fix in **task 70**. Even after 70
  lands, keep this: any future cwd/environment mistake now degrades to "note it, don't
  revert" instead of reverting completed work and getting re-picked forever by
  `selectNextTask` (`src/task-selector.ts:48` returns in-progress tasks ahead of all pending).
- The classifier is deliberately biased toward "can't run". A real test failure whose output
  happens to contain e.g. `not found` will be misclassified as infrastructure and NOT
  reverted. That trade-off is pre-existing (the `not found` entry predates this task) and is
  the correct direction: a false "can't run" costs one unvalidated task, a false "real
  failure" costs an entire round.
- Per round constraints: `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` was NOT modified and `./install.sh` was
  NOT run. The running loop uses the frozen binary, so these changes do not take effect until
  the user unpins and rebuilds after the round.

tasks.title: Per-command cwd resolution in test-validator.ts
tasks.description:
Task #68 pinned validateTaskTests's cwd to path.resolve(projectRoot) (`src/test-validator.ts:97`, with a comment at :93-96 asserting tests are root-relative). That fixed a real bug but was too blunt.

Measured from <root>/src with root-relative commands:
  npm test                          -> exit 0  (npm walks UP, finds root package.json, runs full suite)
  bun run build                     -> exit 0  (same upward walk; script paths resolve from the manifest's dir)
  bun test test/config.test.ts      -> exit 1  (filter matched nothing)
  bun build --compile src/index.ts  -> exit 1  (FileNotFound)
Conclusion: manifest-driven commands ALREADY self-resolve via upward walk; only PATH-ARGUMENT commands break, and only because the path was written relative to the project root.

Implement per-COMMAND (not per-task) resolution: default the cwd to <projectRoot>/<task.directory>; scan each command string for path-shaped arguments; if any fail to resolve from the task dir but DO resolve from the project root, run THAT command from the root. This is a deterministic pre-flight decision made before anything runs.

Do NOT implement try-then-fall-back (run in task dir, re-run at root on failure): it double-runs suites (slow, side-effecting) and cannot distinguish 'wrong cwd' from 'real failure' — precisely the discrimination that already failed and caused this bug. A task can legitimately mix ["npm test", "npx tsc -p tsconfig.json"], so the decision must be independent per entry. Running manifest-driven commands from the task dir is strictly better than root: in a multi-service repo they find the service's own package.json; in a single-package repo they walk up and behave identically.

YOU MUST SETTLE EXPLICITLY what counts as a 'path-shaped argument' and pin it with tests. Anything containing '/', or also bare filenames like foo.test.ts? Too narrow misses `bun test config.test.ts`; too broad misclassifies flags (--outfile, -p) and scoped package names (@scope/pkg). Document the chosen rule in a comment and cover BOTH the included and the excluded shapes in tests.

Keep the resolver PRIVATE to this module — do not export it. `src/health-check.ts` stays root-only: healthCheck is a single project-wide string in cairn.json, #68 was correct there, and it must not change. Preserve the existing directory '/' -> projectRoot behavior (test at ~:261).

TDD: the existing 'cwd resolution' describe block (test/test-validator.test.ts ~:228-289) encodes the OLD root-only contract — in particular 'runs root-relative test commands from projectRoot even when task.directory is a subdir' (~:241) and 'does not resolve test commands against task.directory' (~:274). Those tests are SUPPOSED to go red; rewrite them to the new contract rather than deleting coverage, add cases for the mixed-command case and the path-shape rule, watch them fail, then implement.

Do NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` value and do NOT run `./install.sh` — both are user-managed for this round (the binary is pinned to a frozen copy outside the repo and the health check is redirected to a throwaway outfile). Note the running loop uses the FROZEN binary, so changes you make to the loop's own source do not take effect until the user unpins and rebuilds after the round.

# Task #70 — Per-command cwd resolution in test-validator.ts

## What changed

`src/test-validator.ts` — replaced the blunt `const cwd = path.resolve(projectRoot)` from
task #68 with a per-COMMAND pre-flight decision. Four new **private** (non-exported)
helpers:

- `tokenizeCommand(cmd)` — small char scanner splitting on whitespace, honoring `'`/`"`
  and stripping the quotes. Quoting matters: `sh -c "test -f x"` must yield ONE token
  `test -f x` (which contains spaces and so can never look path-shaped), not three.
- `isPathShaped(token)` — the rule, see below.
- `resolveTaskDir(directory, projectRoot)` — base cwd `<root>/<task.directory>`.
- `resolveCommandCwd(cmd, taskDir, projectRoot)` — returns `projectRoot` iff some
  path-shaped token fails `existsSync` under `taskDir` but succeeds under `projectRoot`;
  otherwise `taskDir`. Short-circuits to `projectRoot` when `taskDir === projectRoot`.

Call site: `taskDir` computed once per task, `cwd = resolveCommandCwd(cmd, ...)` computed
**inside** the loop, once per command. `src/health-check.ts` untouched (still root-only —
`healthCheck` is one project-wide string, #68 was correct there).

## THE PATH-SHAPED RULE (settled explicitly, documented in a comment at the helper)

A whitespace-separated token, surrounding quotes stripped, is path-shaped iff:

- it does **not** start with `-` — excludes flags AND their embedded values (`-p`,
  `--target=bun`, `--outfile=dist/cairn`). Rationale: a flag's value is typically an
  OUTPUT path that need not exist yet, so whether it resolves says nothing about cwd.
- it does **not** start with `@` — excludes scoped package names (`@scope/pkg`).
- **and** either contains `/` (`test/config.test.ts`, `./run.sh`) **or** matches
  `/^[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]\w*$/` — a bare filename with a *letter-leading* extension
  (`config.test.ts`, `tsconfig.json`).

Consequences, both directions covered by tests:
- IN: `test/config.test.ts` (slash), `config.test.ts` (bare + ext — without this,
  `bun test config.test.ts` would be missed by a slash-only rule).
- OUT: `--outfile=only-at-root/out.js`, `@scope/pkg`, bare `build` (extensionless words
  are overwhelmingly subcommands: `npm test`, `bun run build`), `1.2.3` (extension must
  start with a letter, so versions are values not files).

False positives are cheap by construction: a mis-flagged token only changes the cwd if it
*also* happens to resolve from the root and not from the task dir. Nothing changes
otherwise.

## Behavior notes

- **Default is the task dir, not the root.** Manifest-driven commands carry no path
  argument and self-resolve by walking UP to their manifest — from `<root>/<dir>` they
  find the service's own package.json in a multi-service repo, and in a single-package
  repo the upward walk makes root and task dir identical.
- `directory` of `/`, `.`, `''`, or absent → project root (preserves the pre-existing
  `'/'` test).
- A `directory` that doesn't exist (or isn't a directory) → falls back to the root. Added
  because `spawn` with a nonexistent cwd raises ENOENT for *every* command, turning a
  typo in tasks.json into a validation error. New test covers it.
- Deliberately NOT try-then-fall-back, per the task: re-running a failed suite from a
  second cwd double-runs side-effecting tests and cannot distinguish "wrong cwd" from a
  real failure.

## Tests

`test/test-validator.test.ts` — `cwd resolution` block rewritten (4 tests → 13), coverage
added not deleted. TDD confirmed: **7 red before the implementation**, all green after.

Rewritten to the new contract:
- `does not resolve test commands against task.directory` → now
  **`keeps cwd at the task directory when the path argument resolves there`**, expecting
  `passed` where it used to expect `failed`. This is the actual contract flip.
- `runs root-relative test commands from projectRoot even when task.directory is a subdir`
  → retitled **`runs from projectRoot when a path argument resolves only there`**. It
  stayed green through the change (the resolver detects `root-sentinel.txt` as a path arg
  and redirects), which is the point — the #68 regression it guards is still fixed.

New: default-to-task-dir with a no-path-arg command; slash-bearing arg; **mixed command
list decided per command, not per task** (`['test -f sub-only.txt', 'test -f
root-only.txt']` with `directory: 'sub'` → both pass); nonexistent `task.directory`
fallback; and five path-shape cases (flag-with-embedded-path, `@scope/pkg`, bare
extensionless word, bare filename WITH extension, `1.2.3`).

The exclusion tests use the `sh -c "<script>" <decoy>` idiom — args after the script
become `$0`/`$1` and are inert — so each command succeeds ONLY from the task dir while
carrying a decoy token that resolves ONLY from the root. If the decoy were misclassified,
the command would be redirected to the root and fail. That makes them genuinely
discriminating rather than vacuously green.

## Verification

- `bun test test/test-validator.test.ts` → **36 pass, 0 fail** (was 27).
- `bun test` (full suite) → **813 pass, 0 fail**, 29 files.
- Health check `bun build --target=bun src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/...` → clean.
- **End-to-end against this actual repo**: `validateTaskTests` with
  `projectRoot: <root>`, `directory: 'src'`, and
  `tests: ['bun test test/config.test.ts', 'pwd | grep -q "/src$"']` → `passed`. Both
  commands in one task: the first ran from the root (its path arg only resolves there),
  the second from `<root>/src`. That is per-command resolution demonstrated on real
  commands, not just fixtures.

## Notes for the next agent

- The resolver is intentionally private. If something else needs cwd resolution, export
  it deliberately — don't re-derive the path-shape rule in a second place.
- This layers with task #69's `isCantRunError` broadening. Keep both: #70 prevents the
  wrong cwd, #69 ensures that if a cwd/environment mistake still happens, it degrades to
  "note it" instead of reverting completed work.
- Per round constraints: `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` was NOT modified and `./install.sh`
  was NOT run. The running loop uses the frozen binary, so this change does not take
  effect until the user unpins and rebuilds after the round.

tasks.title: Consecutive-revert guard plus blocked-aware run summary
tasks.description:
Third and last layer of the stuck-task fix. It must work even if layers 1 and 2 (tasks 69 and 70) both miss, so do not assume either is in place.

Today `src/commands/run.ts:602` calls `await deps.validateTaskTests({ task, tasksFilePath, projectRoot })` and DISCARDS the return value. When validation returns { status: 'failed' } the task is reverted to in-progress, and selectNextTask (`src/task-selector.ts:48`) returns any in-progress task ahead of all pending work — so the loop re-picks that same task every iteration, forever. Last round this livelocked for three iterations on a task that was already finished.

Add an IN-MEMORY, per-run, per-task counter of consecutive validation reverts. At 2, set the task's status to 'blocked' with an explanatory note (say why: repeated post-iteration validation failure, and which command failed) and let the loop continue to other work. Reset a task's counter when it validates clean.

'blocked' is already fully plumbed — src/tasks-schema.json, the src/types.ts:23 status union and its validation, `cairn task set-status`, the `cairn status` display, and selectNextTask (which already skips blocked tasks). The only new code is the counter plus the summary change.

Do NOT persist the counter as a Task field — that would require types.ts, tasks-schema.json, and generate-tasks.md changes for no benefit; livelocks only matter within a single run, and an in-memory counter resets naturally on restart. The threshold is fixed at 2 — do NOT add a cairn.json knob.

THE COMPLETION FLAG NEEDS ATTENTION or this trades a visible livelock for a silent drop. `src/commands/run.ts:131` tells agents to create the completion flag when tasks.json has 'no remaining pending/in-progress tasks'. A blocked task is NEITHER, so the flag fires, completedByFlag goes true, and the final summary (~:654-673) prints 'ALL TASKS COMPLETE' with a blocked task sitting right there. Make the summary count and report blocked tasks distinctly, including inside the completedByFlag branch, and make the ntfy title/tags reflect it ('tada' is wrong when tasks are blocked).

Write the tests first and watch them fail.

tasks.notes:
# Task #71 — Consecutive-revert guard plus blocked-aware run summary

## What changed (both in `src/commands/run.ts`; tests in `test/commands/run.test.ts`)

### 1. The guard (new step `k2`, right after `validateTaskTests`)

`validateTaskTests`'s return value is no longer discarded. Two new run-scoped locals
alongside `completedByFlag`/`corruptionEvents`:

- `consecutiveReverts: Map<number, number>` — taskId → consecutive `status: 'failed'`
  validations. **In-memory, per-run, not a Task field** (per the task spec — no
  `types.ts` / `tasks-schema.json` / `generate-tasks.md` churn; it resets naturally on
  restart, which is correct because a livelock only exists inside one run).
- `blockedByGuard: Set<number>` — only used as the summary's fallback count if the final
  tasks.json read throws.

Logic:
- `status === 'failed'` → increment. At `REVERT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` (module const, **fixed
  at 2**, deliberately not a `cairn.json` knob) call `deps.blockTask(...)`, log to stdout
  AND to the iteration log, then **delete the counter entry**. Deleting matters: if a
  human unblocks the task mid-run it gets a fresh pair of attempts instead of re-blocking
  on the very first revert.
- `status === 'passed'` → delete the counter entry (clean validation resets).
- `'skipped'` / `'error'` → left untouched on purpose. `'error'` is `isCantRunError` /
  timeout — infrastructure, not evidence the task is stuck (that's task #69's layer), and
  it does **not** revert the task, so it can't livelock. Neither incrementing nor
  resetting is right for it, so it's a no-op.

The `blockTask` call is wrapped in try/catch — a failed write logs and the loop continues
rather than aborting the run.

Note text: `Blocked by cairn after N consecutive post-iteration test validation failures.
Last failing command — <summarizeFailure(validation.message)>`. `validation.message` for
a failure is already `` `${cmd}: ${output.trim().slice(-200)}` `` from
`test-validator.ts`, so the failing command is the prefix. New private helper
`summarizeFailure()` collapses whitespace to one line and caps at 300 chars so the note
stays readable in `cairn status`.

### 2. New dep `blockTask` on `RunRunDeps` (+ exported `BlockTaskOpts`)

`{ tasksFilePath, dataDir, taskId, note }`. Default impl routes through
`mutateTasksFile` from `tasks-file.ts` — the same locked / atomic / snapshotted path
every `cairn task` mutation takes, so this does NOT violate the "no direct writes to
tasks.json" rule. It sets `status = 'blocked'` and appends the note with the standard
` | ` separator. `'blocked'` needed no new plumbing: schema, `types.ts` union,
`set-status`, `cairn status` and `selectNextTask` (which skips it) all already handle it.

### 3. Blocked-aware final summary

`blockedCount` is computed in the `finally` from a fresh `deps.readTasksFile` of
tasks.json, **not** from `blockedByGuard`. That is deliberate — it also catches tasks an
*agent* blocked, and blocked tasks pre-dating this run. Wrapped in try/catch, falling
back to `blockedByGuard.size`. This read intentionally does NOT increment
`corruptionEvents` (the summary line has already been composed by then).

`allClear = completedByFlag && blockedCount === 0` is the new gate everywhere:

- `Tasks blocked: N` line printed whenever `N > 0` (both the flag path and the
  `selectNextTask → null` path).
- `Status: ALL TASKS COMPLETE` only when `allClear`; otherwise, if the flag fired,
  `Status: NO ACTIONABLE TASKS REMAIN — N blocked task(s) need attention`.
- ntfy: `tags` is `tada` only when `allClear`, else `warning`. Title is
  `Cairn - Complete` / `Cairn - Blocked` (new) / `Cairn - Stopped`.
- The narrated/ntfy body has four branches now (all-clear, flag+blocked, no-flag+blocked,
  no-flag).

**Why this mattered:** the agent prompt (`run.ts:131`) tells agents to create the
completion flag when there are "no remaining pending/in-progress tasks". A blocked task
is neither, so the flag fires and the old summary printed ALL TASKS COMPLETE with a
blocked task sitting right there — trading a visible livelock for a silent drop. The
