  point per the CREATE-vs-RESOLVE rule in `src/brand.ts`).

**`src/utils.ts:30-38`** — kept `findDataDir` as-is (unconditional
`join(projectRoot, BRAND.dataDir)`) and corrected the comment per the task's
instruction: it now says explicitly that it COMPOSES the path, does not probe
the filesystem, and returns the same value whether or not the directory exists.
The single-entry-point rationale is retained and sharpened ("so every caller
agrees on one location instead of each spelling the directory name itself").

## Test changes

**`test/narration.test.ts`** — removed the `NONE` helper and every `exists`
predicate; all calls are now the real signatures. Deleted 5 tests that were
vacuous once the discarded predicate was removed (each was byte-identical in
behavior to a sibling, and their titles claimed liveness coverage that the code
never performed):
- socket: "returns the current brand socket when it is already live",
  "ignores a stale /tmp/ralph-tts.sock left by the pre-rename binary",
  "the hook outranks a live socket at the other path"
- pid: "returns the current brand pid file when it exists",
  "ignores a stale /tmp/ralph-tts.pid left by the pre-rename binary"

Surviving tests were retitled to describe what is actually asserted:
- "defaults to the current brand socket when nothing is installed or running"
  → "falls back to the current brand socket when no project root is given"
  (now also pins both `BRAND.socket` and the `/tmp/cairn-tts.sock` literal, so
  a brand-constant regression to a legacy value is still caught — that was the
  only real content of the deleted stale-path tests).
- pid: "defaults to the current brand pid file" → "returns the current brand
  pid file"; "emits no warnings when a stale legacy pid file is present" →
  "emits no warnings".
- The socket "emits no warnings" case lost its third `{exists: () => true}`
  call, which would have collapsed into a duplicate; replaced with a no-hooks
  temp root so it still covers both resolution branches.
- Added block comments to both describes recording that resolution consults one
  input and never probes /tmp — so the next reader doesn't re-add a probe seam.

**`test/utils.test.ts:165-189`** — retitled the three `findDataDir` cases from
resolve/probe language to compose language ("composes <root>/.cairn when the
directory already exists", "...when nothing exists yet", "never composes a
legacy .ralph path, even when one is present on disk"). Assertions unchanged;
they were already true, just described as if a probe were happening.

## What was deliberately NOT touched

- `RunRunDeps.findNarrationSocketPath` (`src/commands/run.ts:299,353,452`) — the
  different, live seam. Untouched. Verified `test/commands/run.test.ts`
  "binds the narration server to the resolved socket, not a hardcoded one"
  still passes in isolation (1 pass, 0 fail).
- `projectRoot` parameter of `findNarrationSocketPath` — load-bearing hook
  resolution, kept.
- `StartNarrationDeps` (checkHealth/sleep) — live, kept.
- `cairn.json` `healthCheck` and `./install.sh` — user-managed for this round.

## Verification

- `bun test test/narration.test.ts test/utils.test.ts` → 43 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test` (full) → **817 pass, 0 fail**, 29 files. Baseline was 822; the
  delta is exactly the 5 deleted vacuous tests (822 − 5 = 817). No test was
  broken by the signature change — the test edits landed first, so nothing was
  still passing a deps object when the parameters were removed.
- `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck` → clean.

## Notes on the TDD step

Worth being explicit, since the task asked for red-first: this deliverable is a
**dead-API deletion**, and there is no red available for it here. Bun strips TS
types without checking, and both signatures took the seam as an *optional*
parameter, so `_deps`-free calls compile and pass identically against the old
code — and `Function.length` is 0 before and after (optional/defaulted params
don't count). The only enforcement of "no caller passes deps" is the type
checker, and this repo has no standalone `tsc` (no typescript devDependency;
the health check is `bun build --compile`, which does not typecheck).

So the order followed was: rewrite the tests to their final truthful form →
run (green, as expected, because the false *titles* were the defect, not
missing behavior) → delete the source seam → re-run (still green). I did not
manufacture an artificial failing assertion (e.g. asserting on
`fn.toString()`) just to produce a red bar; that would have left a brittle
meta-test in the repo permanently.

## For the next agent

- `src/brand.ts:6-12` states the CREATE-vs-RESOLVE standing rule as "must come
  from the value discovery actually found ... rather than from what is actually
  on disk". That phrasing is precise for `findConfigFile()` / `findProjectRoot()`
  (which genuinely probe) but overstated for `findDataDir()` and
  `findNarrationPidFile()`, which are now documented as pure compositions. The
  *rule* still holds unchanged (use the function, never the constant); only the
  "actually on disk" justification is loose for the composing two. `src/brand.ts`
  was outside this task's file scope so I left it alone. Not filed as a task —

tasks.title: Grant the post-task-reviewer git-inspection and per-task test commands
tasks.description:
The post-task reviewer runs via `claude -p` with a fixed `--allowedTools` list and therefore has NO Bash access at all. In print mode there is no permission prompt to answer, so Bash is simply denied — the reviewer can only read the diff text handed to it by `getGitDiff()`. It can never run the task's tests and can never inspect anything outside the supplied diff. This task gives it the minimum needed to actually verify work.

In `spawnPostTaskReviewer` (src/post-task-reviewer.ts, around lines 153-163), the args array currently contains:

    "--allowedTools",
    `Read,Glob,Grep,Edit(${reviewFileRule}),Write(${reviewFileRule})`,

Extend that rule string with:

1. Enumerated git inspection subcommands: `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)`, `Bash(git show:*)`, `Bash(git status:*)`, `Bash(git rev-parse:*)`. NEVER emit `Bash(git:*)` — that would authorize `git commit`, `git push`, and `git reset`.
2. One rule per entry in `opts.task.tests`, which `spawnPostTaskReviewer` already receives. Granting exactly the commands the task declared covers one-off commands (e.g. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json`) that a static config-derived rule would miss.

Handle the absent/empty `tests` case cleanly (no trailing separators, no empty `Bash()` rule).

VERIFIED CLAUDE CODE SEMANTICS — do not re-derive these:
- `Bash(x:*)` is sugar for `Bash(x *)`: a prefix match with a word boundary, so `Bash(ls *)` matches `ls -la` but not `lsof`.
- Compound commands are split on shell operators (`&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `&`, newlines) and EACH subcommand must match a rule independently. So `Bash(git diff:*)` cannot authorize `git diff && rm -rf /`.
- `--allowedTools` and settings `permissions.allow` MERGE additively; neither overrides the other.

Decide and pin with tests what shape to emit for a `tests` entry containing shell operators (e.g. `cd foo && bun test`), given the per-subcommand matching rule above. Document the decision in a comment.

DO NOT change the `reviewFileRule` mechanism or its explanatory comment block (lines ~136-151) — the rule being derived from the same resolved `reviewsDir` the prompt targets is load-bearing, and a mismatch causes silent write denial.

TDD: add failing tests to test/post-task-reviewer.test.ts asserting the emitted `--allowedTools` string, then implement.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json` — its `healthCheck` is pinned to a throwaway outfile and is user-managed for this round.
tasks.notes:
# Task #77 — Grant the post-task-reviewer git-inspection and per-task test commands

## What changed

**`src/post-task-reviewer.ts`**

1. Added module-level `GIT_INSPECTION_RULES` — the five enumerated read-only git
   subcommands (`diff`, `log`, `show`, `status`, `rev-parse`). Comment explains why
   `Bash(git:*)` is never emitted (it would authorize `git commit`/`push`/`reset`,
   letting the reviewer rewrite the work it is reviewing).
2. Added `buildTestCommandRules(tests?: string[])` — turns `opts.task.tests` into
   `Bash(<cmd>:*)` prefix rules. Not exported (tested end-to-end through
   `spawnPostTaskReviewer`'s spawn args; every edge case is reachable by varying
   `task.tests`, so no extra public surface was added).
3. In `spawnPostTaskReviewer`, the inline `--allowedTools` template literal became a
   built `allowedTools` array joined with `,`:
   `Read, Glob, Grep, Edit(rule), Write(rule), <git rules...>, <test rules...>`.
   `reviewFileRule` and its explanatory comment block are untouched.

**`test/post-task-reviewer.test.ts`** — new `describe("Bash allowlist rules")` block
(11 tests) plus updates to the two pre-existing exact-string assertions, which now
include the git rules and `Bash(bun test:*)` (sampleTask declares `tests: ["bun test"]`).

**`CLAUDE.md`** — one-sentence truth-up: the reviewer's allowlist is no longer
*only* `<dataDir>/reviews/**`; that is now specifically its Edit/Write grant, and the
new Bash grants are described.

## The decision that had to be made: compound `tests` entries

A `tests` entry like `cd services/api && bun test` is **split on shell operators**
(`&&`, `||`, `;`, `|`, `&`, newlines) and emitted as one rule per subcommand —
`Bash(cd services/api:*)` + `Bash(bun test:*)` — rather than one whole-string rule.

Rationale (pinned by the test `"splits a compound test command into one rule per
subcommand"`): Claude Code splits a command on those same operators and matches
**each subcommand independently** against the allowlist. A whole-string rule
`Bash(cd services/api && bun test:*)` would therefore never match anything — the
checker never sees that string as a single unit. Splitting is not a widening: the
same per-subcommand rule is what keeps `Bash(bun test:*)` from authorizing
`bun test && rm -rf /`.

## Other behavior pinned by tests

- Absent (`undefined`) or empty `tests` → allowlist ends exactly at the git rules.
  No trailing comma, no `Bash()`.
- Blank/whitespace entries and dangling operators (`"bun test &&"`, `"; ;"`) are
  dropped, not emitted as empty rules.
- Duplicate subcommands across entries are deduped (first occurrence wins, order
  preserved).
- **Commands containing `(`, `)` or `,` are dropped entirely.** Commas separate rules
  inside the `--allowedTools` string and parens delimit each rule, so such a command
  cannot be expressed as one rule; emitting it anyway would parse as a *different,
  possibly broader* grant. Dropping is the safe failure mode — the reviewer just
  loses the ability to run that one command. Worth knowing if a future task declares
  a test like `bun test --filter a,b`: it will silently not be granted.

## Verification

- `bun test test/post-task-reviewer.test.ts` → 44 pass, 0 fail (11 were failing
  before the implementation — written test-first).
- `bun run test` → 827 pass, 0 fail across 29 files.
- Health check `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`
  → clean. `cairn.json` untouched (healthCheck stays pinned to the throwaway outfile).

tasks.title: New src/claude-settings.ts — safe merge helper for .claude/settings.local.json
tasks.description:
Create a new module `src/claude-settings.ts` that merges Cairn's permission rules into a project's `.claude/settings.local.json`. A user may already have this file from plain `claude` usage, so merging must be strictly non-destructive.

Requirements:

1. Read and parse the existing file when present. On MALFORMED JSON, fail loudly (throw or return a clear error) and NEVER clobber the file. Losing a user's hand-built permission list is the worst possible outcome here.
2. Union `permissions.allow` and `permissions.deny` by value, with dedupe. Create the `permissions` object and either array only if missing.
3. PRESERVE every other key untouched — `hooks`, `env`, `model`, `statusLine`, and any key this code does not recognize must round-trip unchanged. Do not drop unknown keys.
4. Write atomically. Follow the temp-file-replace pattern already used by `writeTasksFile()` in `src/tasks-file.ts` (around line 175).
5. Be idempotent: a second run with the same rules adds nothing and reports nothing.
6. Return which rules were actually added, so callers can report them.

DEDUPE DETAIL: Claude Code treats `Bash(x:*)` as sugar for `Bash(x *)` — they are equivalent. Canonicalize that trailing suffix form FOR COMPARISON ONLY so a user who wrote the spaced form does not accumulate an equivalent duplicate. Never rewrite or reformat a user's existing entry. Rules that differ BEFORE the suffix must stay distinct: `Bash(git:*)` and `Bash(git diff:*)` are different rules and both must survive.

CRITICAL TEST ISOLATION: every test must operate in a temp directory. A test that points this code at the real project root would rewrite THIS repository's actual `.claude/settings.local.json`, which currently holds 18 hand-accumulated rules. Never use the real projectRoot in a test.

TDD: create test/claude-settings.test.ts, write failing tests first (fresh-file creation, merge into existing, unknown-key preservation, malformed-JSON refusal, idempotency, suffix-equivalent dedupe), then implement.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json`.
tasks.notes:
# Task #79 — src/claude-settings.ts safe-merge helper

## Files added

- `src/claude-settings.ts` (new module, no other src file changed)
- `test/claude-settings.test.ts` (new, 28 tests)

`src/tasks-file.ts` was listed in the task's `files` but is **reference only** —
the atomic-write pattern was copied from `writeTasksFile()` (line 175). No edit
was needed there and none was made.

## Public API

```ts
class ClaudeSettingsError extends Error            // thrown on unparseable/misshapen input
interface PermissionRules { allow?: string[]; deny?: string[] }
interface MergeResult {
  created: boolean;        // true only when this call created the file
  addedAllow: string[];    // rules actually appended, in supplied order & original spelling
  addedDeny: string[];
  settingsPath: string;    // absolute path targeted
}

claudeSettingsPath(projectRoot): string            // <root>/.claude/settings.local.json
canonicalizeRule(rule): string                     // comparison key ONLY, never written
mergeClaudeSettings(projectRoot, rules): MergeResult
```

Signature note for the caller task: it takes **projectRoot**, not a file path.
It computes `.claude/settings.local.json` itself and `mkdir -p`s `.claude/`.

## Behavior decisions worth knowing

1. **Malformed JSON → throw, never write.** `readSettings()` runs *before* any
   other decision, so a broken file is an error even when there was nothing to
   add (`{allow: []}` against a garbage file still throws). Rationale: silently
   succeeding would leave a broken permission list unnoticed until it denied
   something. Every error message names the full file path and says Cairn will
   not overwrite it.
2. **Shape validation, not just parse validation.** Also throws when the top
   level isn't a JSON object, when `permissions` isn't an object, or when
   `permissions.allow` / `permissions.deny` isn't an array. Anything we can't
   confidently interpret is refused rather than clobbered.
3. **Suffix canonicalization is Bash-only and comparison-only.**
   `canonicalizeRule` maps `Bash(x:*)` → `Bash(x *)` and leaves everything else
   verbatim. Deliberately *not* applied to other tools — collapsing `Read(x:*)`
   into `Read(x *)` could merge two genuinely different rules; there's a test
   asserting they stay distinct. Only the trailing suffix is touched, so
   `Bash(git:*)` and `Bash(git diff:*)` remain separate rules (tested). The
   user's own spelling is never rewritten on disk — if they wrote `Bash(bun *)`
   and we supply `Bash(bun:*)`, nothing is added and their string stays as-is.
   `.trim()` is applied for comparison so leading/trailing whitespace in a
   hand-edited entry doesn't create a phantom duplicate.
4. **No-write idempotency.** When `addedAllow` and `addedDeny` are both empty,
   the function returns early and does **not** touch the file at all — a test
   asserts a compact one-line JSON file keeps its exact original bytes after a
   no-op merge. So mtime/formatting are preserved on repeat runs.
5. **Unknown-key preservation via spread**, at both levels: top-level
   (`hooks`, `env`, `model`, `statusLine`, arbitrary future keys) and inside
   `permissions` (`defaultMode`, `additionalDirectories`, ...). Since
   `permissions` already exists in the object when present, the spread also
   preserves its original key *position* in the file.
6. **Arrays created only when needed.** `permissions` is created only if
   missing; `allow` is only written when something was added to it, likewise
   `deny`. Merging one allow rule into a deny-only file leaves `deny` alone and
   does not invent an empty array anywhere.
7. **Non-string entries** in a user's `allow` array are preserved on write but
   skipped for matching (they can't equal any rule).
8. **Atomic write**, mirroring `writeTasksFile()`: stage to
   `<path>.tmp.<pid>.<6 random hex bytes>`, then `renameSync` over the target;
   `unlink` the temp file if anything throws. Output is `JSON.stringify(x, null, 2)`
   plus a trailing newline. A test asserts `.claude/` contains only
   `settings.local.json` after two merges (no temp residue).

## Test isolation

Every test runs in `fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir(), 'cairn-claude-settings-test-')`
and rmrf's it in `afterEach`. The real `projectRoot` is never used — there is a
comment at the top of the test file saying why. Verified after the run:
`git status --short .claude/` is empty and the repo's own
`settings.local.json` still holds its 18 hand-accumulated rules.

## Verification

- `bun test test/claude-settings.test.ts` → 28 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run test` → **855 pass, 0 fail** across 30 files (was 827/29 before)
- Health check `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`
  → compiles clean (throwaway outfile per the pinned-binary procedure)
- `cairn.json` not modified, as instructed.

## For the next agent

This module has **no callers yet** — it is pure library code. The follow-up task
that wires it in should call
`mergeClaudeSettings(projectRoot, { allow: [...] })` (probably from
`src/commands/init.ts`) and report `result.addedAllow` / `result.addedDeny` to
the user; both being empty is the "already up to date, say nothing" signal.
`ClaudeSettingsError` should surface to the user as-is — its message is already
written to be read by a human and explains the manual fix.

tasks.title: Wire the settings.local.json writer into cairn init
tasks.description:
Use the merge helper from `src/claude-settings.ts` (task #79) to seed a permission baseline during `cairn init`.

In `runInit` (src/commands/init.ts, around line 472), add a step alongside the existing `installNarrationHooks` and `createInstructionsFile` prompts. PROMPT the user before writing, DEFAULTING TO YES — use the existing `promptBoolean` helper. Writing permission rules affects every Claude session in that project, so it gets a visible confirmation.

Rule set to merge:

ALLOW:
- Git inspection subcommands: `Bash(git diff:*)`, `Bash(git log:*)`, `Bash(git show:*)`, `Bash(git status:*)`, `Bash(git rev-parse:*)`. Never a blanket `Bash(git:*)`.
- Rules derived from the project's `cairn.json` values for `healthCheck` and `defaultTestCommand` (available from the config object init already builds). Skip cleanly when a value is empty.

DENY — exactly these five, no more:
- `Bash(cairn task start:*)`
- `Bash(cairn task complete:*)`
- `Bash(cairn task set-status:*)`
- `Bash(cairn task add:*)`
- `Bash(cairn task note:*)`

NEVER emit a blanket `Bash(cairn task:*)` deny. `commands/generate-tasks.md:149` requires `cairn task next-id` for ID allocation, deny beats allow regardless of specificity, and there is no mechanism to carve an exception back out — a blanket deny would silently break task generation in every project. `next-id` and `show` must remain allowed.

These denies exist because the reviewer's inability to mutate `tasks.json` previously depended on it having no Bash at all; task #77 removes that implicit lock. Denies bind the reviewer and planner but are bypassed by `cairn run` execution agents (which use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`), which is exactly the intended scoping.

GITIGNORE: print a WARNING telling the user to gitignore `.claude/settings.local.json` themselves. Claude Code only auto-ignores that file when Claude Code itself writes it, and the entry goes to the user's GLOBAL git excludes, not the repo — so a file Cairn creates first gets no ignore entry. Do NOT edit any `.gitignore` and do NOT touch global git config.

Report written rules using the existing `InstallOptions` / `skipUnchanged` / `log` reporting style used by `writeNarrationHooks` and `installMdDir`.

CRITICAL TEST ISOLATION: tests must use a temp projectRoot. Never point init at the real repository root — this repo's `.claude/settings.local.json` has 18 accumulated rules.

TDD against test/commands/init.test.ts. DO NOT modify `cairn.json`.
tasks.notes:
# Task #80 — Wire the settings.local.json writer into `cairn init`

## What changed

- `src/commands/init.ts` — new `buildInitPermissionRules()` + `installClaudeSettings()`,
  called from `runInit()` after `installNarrationHooks`, before `showNextSteps`.
- `src/claude-settings.ts` — added two exports used by both callers:
  `GIT_INSPECTION_RULES` and `buildCommandRules()`.
- `src/post-task-reviewer.ts` — **not in the task's file list**, edited anyway to
  delete its private copies of those two things and import the shared ones. See
  "Why post-task-reviewer.ts was touched" below.
- `test/commands/init.test.ts` — 24 new tests.
- `CLAUDE.md` — one sentence noting the rule builders are now shared.
- `src/config.ts` was in the task's file list but needed **no change**: `runInit`
  already has the fully-resolved `CairnConfig` in hand from `promptForConfig`.

## Public API added to init.ts

```ts
buildInitPermissionRules(config: Pick<CairnConfig, 'healthCheck' | 'defaultTestCommand'>): PermissionRules
installClaudeSettings(projectRoot, config, rl, opts?: InstallOptions): Promise<string[]>
```

`installClaudeSettings` returns the rules it actually added (allow then deny);
`[]` means declined, already-complete, or unreadable existing file. The narrowed
`Pick<...>` param type is deliberate — it documents that only two config fields
feed the rules, and lets tests build a two-field literal instead of a whole
`CairnConfig`.

## Rules written

Allow: the five read-only git subcommands, plus `Bash(<cmd>:*)` for each
subcommand of `healthCheck` and `defaultTestCommand`. Deny: exactly the five
task-mutating `cairn task` subcommands. Empty config values contribute nothing;
duplicates between healthCheck and defaultTestCommand collapse to one rule.

**Do not ever collapse the denies into `Bash(cairn task:*)`.** `commands/generate-tasks.md:149`
needs `cairn task next-id`, deny beats allow regardless of specificity, and there
is no way to carve an exception back out — a blanket deny silently breaks task
generation in every initialized project. There is a test asserting no deny rule
mentions `next-id` or `show`, and one asserting the deny array equals exactly the
five rules. Same for `Bash(git:*)` on the allow side (also tested).

## Decisions worth knowing

1. **Prompt defaults to YES** (`[Y/n]`), per the task. It writes an intro block
   explaining what gets allowed/denied and that existing rules are preserved.
2. **`ClaudeSettingsError` is caught, not propagated.** Task #79's notes said the
   message should "surface to the user as-is" — it does, printed verbatim — but
   letting it escape `runInit` would abort init with a stack trace *after*
   `cairn.json` was already written. Report and continue. Tested: a `{ not json`
   file is left byte-identical and `Refusing to modify` is printed.
3. **`InstallOptions.skipUnchanged` is accepted but never consulted**, and the
   doc comment says so. Merging is inherently additive — an already-present rule
   is never rewritten and never reported, so the flag has no meaning here. The
   type is reused for `log` so the installer family stays consistent.
4. **The gitignore WARNING prints only when rules were actually written.** On a
   re-run that adds nothing, the merge doesn't touch the file, so there's no
   warning to repeat. No `.gitignore` is created or edited and git config is not
   touched — both asserted by tests.

## Why post-task-reviewer.ts was touched

It held a private `GIT_INSPECTION_RULES` array and a private
`buildTestCommandRules()` whose body was exactly the splitter this task needed.
Copying either into init.ts would have created two independently-editable copies
of a security-sensitive allowlist that must agree. Both moved to
`claude-settings.ts`; `buildTestCommandRules` survives as a one-line delegation
so the reviewer's own call sites and tests are unchanged. Existing reviewer tests
(`test/post-task-reviewer.test.ts:224`, `:420-424`) still pin the exact git rule
string and pass untouched.

The shared splitter keeps the reviewer's stricter `/[(),]/` filter even though
commas are harmless inside a JSON array (they only break the reviewer's
comma-separated `--allowedTools` string). Sharing the stricter filter can only
ever drop an exotic rule, never widen one — noted in the comment.

## Verification

- `bun test test/commands/init.test.ts` → 135 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run test` → **879 pass, 0 fail** across 30 files (was 855 before)
- Health check `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck` → clean
- Manual smoke run of `installClaudeSettings` against a temp dir: verified the
  printed report, the on-disk JSON, and that a second run prints
  "already has every rule" and writes nothing.
- `cairn.json` not modified (still pinned to the throwaway outfile).

## Trap for the next agent — `runInit` prompt counting

`allDefaultAnswers()` in the runInit describe block returns **9** answers but
`runInit` asks **11** questions with narration disabled (10 config + instructions).
`createMockPrompt` returns `''` past the end of the array, so the array is already
short and the trailing `'n'` in it lands on `reviewMaxIterations`, not on the
instructions prompt. Appending an answer to `allDefaultAnswers()` therefore does
**not** target the last prompt. The "skips the settings file when the user
declines" test spells out all 12 answers explicitly instead — do the same for any
new prompt rather than trusting that helper's name.

## Test isolation

Every new test uses `fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir(), ...)` and rm -rf's in
`afterEach`. Verified after the run: `git status --short .claude/` is clean and
this repo's own `.claude/settings.local.json` (18 hand-accumulated rules, and
gitignored) is untouched.

One caveat learned the hard way: running `cairn init` from a scratch directory
under `/tmp` **still resolved projectRoot back to this repository** and
re-installed `.claude/commands/*` and `.claude/agents/*` over the repo's copies
(reverted via `git checkout --`). Do not smoke-test `init` end-to-end by cd'ing
to a temp dir; call the exported function with an explicit temp `projectRoot`.

tasks.title: CLAUDE.md — truth-up the tasks.json enforcement story
tasks.description:
Two corrections to `CLAUDE.md`'s "Agent workflow" section.

1. THE ENFORCEMENT SET IS NOW WRONG. CLAUDE.md says direct `Edit`/`Write` on `tasks.json` is "enforced two ways: the per-agent system prompt explicitly bans it, and the post-task reviewer runs with a directory-scoped allowlist covering only `<dataDir>/reviews/**`". There was an unstated THIRD lock: the reviewer had no Bash at all, so it could not run `cairn task set-status` either. Task #77 removes that lock by granting the reviewer git-inspection subcommands and the reviewed task's test commands.

   Document the actual enforcement set as it now stands: the prompt ban, the directory-scoped write allowlist, and the explicit `permissions.deny` rules on the five mutating `cairn task` subcommands that `cairn init` writes (task #80). Record two facts that are easy to get wrong:
   - Deny rules are NOT enforced under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, so they do not bind `cairn run` execution agents. They bind the reviewer and planner, which run in normal permission mode. This asymmetry is intended.
   - The deny covers mutating subcommands ONLY. A blanket `Bash(cairn task:*)` would break `cairn task next-id`, which task generation requires; deny beats allow with no exception mechanism.

2. SCOPE THE BAN ITSELF. "Direct `Edit` or `Write` on `tasks.json` is forbidden" currently contradicts `commands/generate-tasks.md:159`, which explicitly instructs the planning session to write `.cairn/tasks.json` using the Write tool. Both are right in intent — the ban targets EXECUTION AGENTS mutating a live task list mid-round, whereas task generation authors the file wholesale between rounds. Add a clause saying so, so the two documents stop contradicting each other.

CRITICAL GUARD — DO NOT MODIFY `cairn.json`. Its `healthCheck` is currently pinned to a throwaway outfile (`bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile /tmp/cairn-healthcheck`) and is USER-MANAGED for this round. CLAUDE.md documents the REAL value (`bun run build` / `bun build --compile src/index.ts --outfile dist/cairn`) and must continue to. While the round runs, CLAUDE.md and `cairn.json` will legitimately disagree about the health check. That disagreement is EXPECTED and must NOT be "fixed" in either direction. In a previous round exactly this trap caused the pinned value to be committed permanently.

tasks.title: Add same-task stall guard to the run loop
tasks.description:
A recent bug caused `cairn run` to burn 60 iterations re-assigning the same task, every iteration reporting SUCCESS, because the execution agent was blocked from calling `cairn task start`/`complete` by a permissions deny rule. The task stayed `pending`, so the loop re-selected it forever. Add a guard so this announces itself in 3 iterations instead of 60.

Practice TDD: write the failing test first, watch it fail, then implement.

IMPLEMENTATION:

1. Add `const STALL_BLOCK_THRESHOLD = 3;` near the existing `REVERT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` (around `src/commands/run.ts:389`). Hardcode it — do NOT add a `cairn.json` config key. Add a brief comment saying it is deliberately not configurable, matching the `REVERT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` precedent: three identical no-op iterations is unambiguous, and a misconfigured value would re-hide the failure.

2. Add an in-memory `Map<number, number>` counter for the run, declared alongside `consecutiveReverts` (around `src/commands/run.ts:478`). In-memory per-run is correct — a livelock only matters within a single run.

3. PREDICATE (important, get this exact): increment the counter for a task only when it was selected while `status === 'pending'` AND is still `pending` on the post-iteration re-read of tasks.json — meaning the agent never called `cairn task start` at all. Any other observed status (`in-progress`, `complete`, `blocked`) RESETS the counter to zero. If the tasks.json re-read throws, treat it as neutral: no increment and no reset. Do NOT use a looser "status did not change" predicate — a task legitimately sitting in `in-progress` across several iterations is normal and must not trip the guard.

4. REQUIRED REFACTOR: the post-iteration status re-read currently lives INSIDE the `if (config.review?.postTask)` block at `src/commands/run.ts:678-690`. Hoist it out so it runs unconditionally, otherwise the guard silently does nothing whenever post-task review is disabled. Preserve the existing behavior of incrementing `corruptionEvents` when the read result reports `repaired || restored`, and keep passing the resulting status into the existing review gate at `run.ts:692` unchanged.

5. On reaching the threshold, mirror the revert-guard block at `src/commands/run.ts:659-672`: call `deps.blockTask({ tasksFilePath, dataDir, taskId, note })`, log a loud message, append a line to the iteration log, clear that task's counter, and continue to the next task (do NOT halt the whole run). The note must name the likely cause so a future user does not have to re-debug it — something like: blocked after N consecutive iterations in which the agent never moved the task out of `pending`; the usual cause is a `permissions.deny` rule for `cairn task` in `.claude/settings.local.json`, which is NOT bypassed by `--dangerously-skip-permissions`.

TESTS: add to `test/commands/run.test.ts`, modelling them on the existing revert-guard tests around lines 1170-1260. Cover: (a) three consecutive pending-after-iteration selections trigger `blockTask`; (b) an intervening `in-progress` or `complete` status resets the counter so no block occurs; (c) a throwing tasks.json read neither increments nor resets; (d) the hoisted status read still feeds the post-task review gate correctly when review is enabled, and the guard still works when `review.postTask` is false.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` value and DO NOT run `./install.sh`. The user has pinned the installed binary and redirected the health check to a throwaway outfile for the duration of this round; both are user-managed.

# Task #85 — Same-task stall guard in the run loop

## What changed

`src/commands/run.ts`:

1. **`STALL_BLOCK_THRESHOLD = 3`** added directly under `REVERT_BLOCK_THRESHOLD`, with a
   comment stating it is deliberately not configurable (same reasoning as the revert
   threshold: three identical no-op iterations are unambiguous, and a misconfigured
   value would re-hide the failure). No `cairn.json` key was added.

2. **`consecutiveStalls: Map<number, number>`** declared right after `consecutiveReverts`
   in `runRun`. In-memory, per-run.

3. **`selectedStatus` snapshot** captured immediately after task selection (next to
   `const taskDir = ...`). The guard compares against this snapshot rather than
   re-reading `task.status` after the agent has run. In production `readTasksFile`
   re-parses fresh objects each iteration so `task` is already a snapshot, but the
   test fixtures share one mutable array, and a future refactor could too — reading
   the field back post-spawn would be a latent aliasing bug.

4. **REQUIRED REFACTOR done**: the post-iteration status re-read was hoisted out of
   `if (config.review?.postTask)` into new unconditional step `k3`. `corruptionEvents++`
   on `repaired || restored` is preserved, and the resulting `updatedTaskStatus` still
   feeds the review gate unchanged. The review gate collapsed from a nested
   `if (postTask) { if (complete) }` to a single `&&`.

5. **Guard block `k4`**, mirroring the revert guard at `k2`: on threshold it calls
   `deps.blockTask({ tasksFilePath, dataDir, taskId, note })`, logs loudly, appends a
   `BLOCKED` line to the iteration log, clears that task's counter, and falls through
   to the next iteration (the run is *not* halted). The note names the likely cause:
   a `permissions.deny` rule for `cairn task` in `.claude/settings.local.json`, which
   `--dangerously-skip-permissions` does NOT bypass.

## The predicate (exact semantics implemented)

- Increment **only** when `selectedStatus === 'pending'` AND the post-iteration
  re-read also reports `'pending'` — i.e. the agent never ran `cairn task start`.
- Any other *observed* status (`in-progress`, `complete`, `blocked`) resets the
  counter to zero. This is deliberately not a "status did not change" check: a task
  legitimately parked in `in-progress` across several iterations is normal and must
  not trip the guard.
- A throwing re-read (or a task missing from the list) leaves `updatedTaskStatus` at
  the sentinel `'unknown'` → neither increment nor reset.
- Edge case, intentional: selected as `in-progress` but observed `pending` (agent
  moved it backwards) is neither an increment nor a reset.

## Tests (`test/commands/run.test.ts`, new `--- Same-task stall guard ---` section)

Seven tests, reusing the existing `makeGuardDeps` fixture from the revert-guard suite:

- three pending-after-iteration selections block task 1 and the loop moves on to
  finish task 2 (asserts `spawnClaude` called 4×, note contains `pending` and
  `permissions.deny`); runs with review disabled, proving the hoist matters
- an intervening `in-progress` resets — 6 iterations, no block
- an intervening `complete` resets to zero — asserts the block lands at iteration 5,
  not 4, which is the discriminating assertion (a missing reset blocks at 4)
- a throwing post-iteration read is neutral — asserts the block lands at iteration 4;
  an increment would block at 3, a reset would push it to 6
- the iteration log gets the `BLOCKED` line
- the hoisted read still feeds the review gate (`taskStatus === 'complete'`)
- the guard still fires with `review.postTask` enabled

TDD followed: tests written first, 5 of 7 failed (the two review/in-progress cases
pass trivially against the old code), then implemented to green.

tasks.title: Delete CAIRN_TASK_DENY_RULES from init's permission seeding
tasks.description:
`cairn init` seeds `.claude/settings.local.json` with a project-wide `deny` list covering five mutating `cairn task` subcommands. The result was a loop that ran 60 iterations without ever recording a completion. The rules were also never necessary: in headless `claude -p` mode, anything with side effects is deny-by-default unless allowlisted (there is nobody to prompt), so the reviewer's scoped `--allowedTools` already prevented task-state mutation. Delete the deny rules; keep the allow rules, which were the genuine fix for health checks and reviewer tests failing.

Practice TDD: invert the existing assertions FIRST, watch them fail, then delete the code.

NEW ASSERTIONS: `buildInitPermissionRules(...)` returns no `deny` (absent or empty), and a freshly seeded `settings.local.json` contains no `cairn task` deny entry while the allow list (git inspection rules plus health-check and test-command rules) is unchanged.

tasks.title: Init migration: strip a legacy cairn task deny block on re-run
tasks.description:
Any project initialized by the previous version of `cairn init` has a `deny` block in `.claude/settings.local.json` that silently breaks `cairn run` — every execution agent is blocked from `cairn task start`/`complete`, so tasks never leave `pending` and the loop re-runs the same task indefinitely while reporting SUCCESS. That file is gitignored, so nothing in `git status` reveals it. Re-running `cairn init` must repair such a project.

Practice TDD: write the failing tests first.

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Add a removal counterpart to the existing additive merge in `src/claude-settings.ts` — e.g. `removeSettingsRules(projectRoot, rules)`. Compare rules using the existing `canonicalizeRule` helper so both `Bash(cairn task start:*)` and spaced/otherwise-equivalent forms are matched.
2. Required behavior: preserve every other key in the settings file byte-for-byte where possible; preserve any unrelated user-authored deny entries (remove ONLY the five `cairn task` rules); drop the `deny` key entirely when removal empties it; write through the existing atomic-replace path used by the additive merge; no-op cleanly when the file does not exist or is already clean; and surface `ClaudeSettingsError` for a malformed/unparseable file rather than overwriting it.
3. Call it from `installClaudeSettings` and report to the user what was removed, alongside the existing reporting of what was added.

The five legacy rules: `Bash(cairn task start:*)`, `Bash(cairn task complete:*)`, `Bash(cairn task set-status:*)`, `Bash(cairn task add:*)`, `Bash(cairn task note:*)`.

TESTS: `test/claude-settings.test.ts` and `test/commands/init.test.ts`. Cover a file with only the legacy rules, a file mixing legacy and unrelated user deny rules, an already-clean file, a missing file, and a malformed file.

*** CRITICAL HAZARD — READ BEFORE RUNNING ANYTHING ***
Exercise this code ONLY against throwaway temp directories created with `mkdtempSync`, following the existing pattern at `test/commands/init.test.ts:36` and throughout that file. NEVER run `cairn init`, `installClaudeSettings`, or this migration against this repository's own root. # Task #87 — Init migration: strip a legacy cairn task deny block on re-run

## What changed

### `src/claude-settings.ts` (new: `removeSettingsRules`)

- New exported `RemovalResult { removedAllow, removedDeny, settingsPath }`.
- New private `partitionRules(existing, targets)` — splits a rule array into
  `kept` (unknown values preserved verbatim, including non-strings) and
  `removed`. Matching is by `canonicalizeRule`, so `Bash(cairn task start:*)`,
  `Bash(cairn task start *)` and whitespace-padded spellings all match. Removed
  entries are reported **in the spelling found on disk**, not the spelling
  searched for, so init can tell the user what it actually took out.
- New exported `removeSettingsRules(projectRoot, rules)` — mirror of
  `mergeClaudeSettings`:
  - reuses the same `readSettings()` validator (so a malformed / non-object /
    non-array-permissions file throws `ClaudeSettingsError` and is never
    rewritten) and the same `writeSettingsAtomic()` temp-file + rename path;
  - no-ops without writing when the file is absent, when nothing matches, or
    when handed an empty rule set;
  - spreads top-level and `permissions` objects, so unknown keys
    (`model`, `hooks`, `defaultMode`, `additionalDirectories`, …) round-trip;
  - **deletes** the `allow`/`deny` key entirely when removal empties it rather
    than leaving `[]` behind;
  - only touches a list it was given rules for (`{deny: [...]}` never rewrites
    `allow`, even if an identical rule sits in `allow`).

### `src/commands/init.ts`

- New exported `LEGACY_CAIRN_TASK_DENY_RULES` (the five `cairn task` rules)
  with a doc comment explaining *why* they are destructive rather than merely
  obsolete (project-wide deny binds `cairn run` execution agents, not bypassed
  by `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, file is gitignored so `git status` shows
  nothing).
- `installClaudeSettings` now calls `removeSettingsRules` **before**
  `mergeClaudeSettings`, inside the same try/catch — so a malformed file is
  reported once via the existing `ClaudeSettingsError` path and neither
  operation writes.
- Reporting: removals are printed (`Removed a legacy deny block from …`, one
  `deny:  <rule>` line each, plus a two-line explanation of the symptom) above
  the existing added-rules report. The `already has every rule.` line is now
  suppressed when a removal happened (otherwise a repair run would print
  "already has every rule", which is misleading).

tasks.title: CLAUDE.md: correct the tasks.json enforcement story
tasks.description:
The "Agent workflow" section of `CLAUDE.md` currently claims the ban on direct `tasks.json` mutation is "enforced three ways", and states as fact that `permissions.deny` rules are not enforced under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. That claim is FALSE and is the direct cause of a bug that cost 60 wasted loop iterations: the deny rules DID bind `cairn run`'s execution agents, blocking every `cairn task start`/`complete` call so no task ever left `pending`.

EDIT `CLAUDE.md` to tell the true story:

1. Replace "enforced three ways" with the two mechanisms that are actually real:
   - The per-agent system prompt ban. State plainly that this is the ONLY constraint on execution agents, because they run with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. This was always true; the old text obscured it.
   - Per-agent `--allowedTools` scoping, which is effective precisely BECAUSE headless mode is deny-by-default. This covers the reviewer and planner. The reviews-directory write scoping described in the existing mechanism 2 is genuine and should be kept.
2. DELETE the third mechanism (the `permissions.deny` rules written by `cairn init`) and DELETE both "facts about the deny rules that are easy to get wrong" bullets, including the false `--dangerously-skip-permissions` claim.
3. State the governing rule explicitly: in headless `claude -p`, anything with side effects is denied by default unless allowlisted, because there is no interactive session to prompt for approval. Only side-effect-free commands pass without a grant.
4. Record the supporting evidence so this is never re-derived from intuition. Three empirical probes established it: (a) a project-level deny rule blocked a command even under `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; (b) a non-allowlisted Bash command writing inside the working directory was blocked; (c) a `Write` outside the granted `Edit(...)` scope was blocked, with the agent reporting that the session was non-interactive so it could not prompt. Note also the trap that a bare `echo` DOES run without a grant — it is side-effect-free, so it proves nothing about commands that write.

KEEP UNCHANGED: the paragraph explaining why task generation is exempt from the direct-write ban (`commands/generate-tasks.md` legitimately writes `tasks.json` between rounds), and the paragraph about `writeTasksFile()`'s atomic replacement and JSON validation. Keep the note that `cairn task next-id` and `show` must stay reachable — it documents why a blanket deny reflex fails.

This is a documentation-only task. Do not change any source code.

DO NOT modify `cairn.json`'s `healthCheck` and DO NOT run `./install.sh` — both are user-pinned for this round.

tasks.description:
Create `src/run-state.ts`: a small, locked, atomic store for round runtime state, persisted in a gitignored temp file inside the data dir.

CONTEXT: guard counters (reverts, stalls, and a new 'incompletes') are currently in-memory Maps inside runRun (src/commands/run.ts). Under the new `/cairn-run` mode the loop driver is a model that can be compacted, resumed or restarted, so counters and per-task attempt data must live on disk. Later tasks (93+) wire this store in; this task only builds and tests it.

FILE: path via `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'run_state.json')` (src/utils.ts), i.e. `.cairn_run_state.json`. Callers pass an already-resolved dataDir (from findDataDir) — never rebuild the path from BRAND.dataDir (CLAUDE.md convention: BRAND constants are for creating paths, discovery for resolving them).

SHAPE (export the types RunState, AttemptRecord, AttemptPhase):
{ iteration: number, attempts: { [taskId: string]: { beforeSha: string | null, iteration: number, reverts: number, stalls: number, incompletes: number, phase: 'executing' | 'awaiting-review' } } }

API (suggested names):
- `readRunState(dataDir): RunState` — missing file returns `{ iteration: 0, attempts: {} }`; an unparseable file is treated as empty and does not throw (runtime state is disposable).
- `updateRunState(dataDir, fn: (state) => T): T` — acquire `acquireLock(<statePath>.lock)` from src/file-lock.ts, read, apply fn (mutating the state), write atomically (unique temp file + rename, mirroring writeTasksFile in src/tasks-file.ts), and in a finally block close the fd and unlink the lock. Returns fn's result. The lock must be released when fn throws.
- Convenience helpers such as `getAttempt(dataDir, taskId)` and `clearAttempt(dataDir, taskId)`.

LOCKING RULES — document these in the module header comment; later tasks rely on them:
- Critical sections must be SHORT. acquireLock treats a lock older than 60s as stale and breaks it, while test validation can run 120s per command. Never hold the run-state lock across test validation, agent execution or health checks; do read-modify-write in short updateRunState calls.
- acquireLock is not reentrant. Lock ordering: the run-state lock may be taken before the tasks.json lock (mutateTasksFile takes `tasks.json.lock` internally), never the reverse — never call updateRunState from inside a mutateTasksFile callback.

GITIGNORE (required): add `'run_state.json'` and `'run_state.json.lock'` to `TEMP_IGNORE_SUFFIXES` in src/commands/init.ts, and update the expected ignore-block lines asserted in test/commands/init.test.ts (around lines 70-100).

TESTS: `test/run-state.test.ts`, all in temp dirs (fs.mkdtempSync): empty default; write/read round-trip; updateRunState returns fn's value; a corrupt file is tolerated; the lock file is gone after an update; the lock is released when fn throws.

TEMP DIRS ONLY: never run `cairn init` or the init/claude-settings functions against this repository's root; exercise them only in temp directories created by the tests (fs.mkdtempSync).

# Task #92: Run-state store (src/run-state.ts)

## What was built

`src/run-state.ts` — a small, locked, atomic store for round runtime state,
persisted to `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'run_state.json')` (`.cairn_run_state.json`)
inside the caller's already-resolved dataDir.

Exports:
- Types: `RunState` (`{ iteration, attempts: { [taskId]: AttemptRecord } }`),
  `AttemptRecord` (`{ beforeSha, iteration, reverts, stalls, incompletes, phase }`),
  `AttemptPhase` (`'executing' | 'awaiting-review'`).
- `readRunState(dataDir)` — missing file → `{ iteration: 0, attempts: {} }`;
  unparseable/malformed file → same empty default, never throws.
- `updateRunState(dataDir, fn)` — acquires `acquireLock(<statePath>.lock)`,
  reads current state, runs `fn(state)` (may mutate in place and/or return a
  value), writes the result back atomically (unique tmp path + rename,
  mirroring `writeTasksFile`), and in a `finally` closes the fd and unlinks
  the lock — released even when `fn` throws. Returns `fn`'s return value.
- `getAttempt(dataDir, taskId)` / `clearAttempt(dataDir, taskId)` —
  convenience helpers; `clearAttempt` goes through `updateRunState` so it's
  itself locked/atomic.

critical sections given the 60s stale-lock threshold vs. up to 120s test
validation; non-reentrant `acquireLock`, and lock ordering — run-state lock

Define the settle verdict contract and make settle idempotent based on the attempt record.

CONTEXT: settleTask (src/settle.ts) validates, applies guards and persists counters in the run-state attempt record (src/run-state.ts; tasks 91/93, and task 94 adds `retryMode` and the incomplete guard — if 94 has landed, build on its retryMode). 1. Exported Verdict union (the CLI will print it as JSON):
- `{ verdict: 'retry', taskId, mode: 'continue' | 'fresh', reason, failure?, next }` — `failure` gets the last ~40 lines of test output from task 96; keep it optional.
- `{ verdict: 'blocked', taskId, reason, next }` — a guard block, or the agent itself set status 'blocked' (reason taken from the task's notes; clear the record).
- `{ verdict: 'done', taskId, reason?, next }` — task 97 adds reasons such as 'review-disabled' | 'no-commits' | 'no-before-sha' | 'reviewed'.
- `{ verdict: 'already-settled', taskId, next }`.
(Task 97 adds a `review` verdict.) Every verdict has `next`, a short imperative hint for the driver: 'Run: cairn round next' for done/blocked/already-settled; for retry/continue 'Resume the same task agent with SendMessage, then run: cairn round settle <id>' (and say: if that agent's id is lost, launch a fresh cairn-task-agent instead); for retry/fresh 'Launch a fresh cairn-task-agent with the same prompt file, then run: cairn round settle <id>'.
2. Retry mode mapping: stall → fresh; incompletes 1 → continue, 2 → fresh; failed validation below the revert threshold → continue.
3. Idempotency keyed on the ATTEMPT RECORD, not on archived status (task 97 makes settle archive before its review gate, so a status-based check would swallow later calls):
- No record, task id absent from tasks.json but present in tasks.completed.json → `already-settled`, no side effects.
- No record, task present in tasks.json → create the record lazily (beforeSha null for now — task 97 adds a commit-message fallback; iteration from run state) and proceed normally.
- Unknown id (in neither file) → throw a typed `SettleError`.
4. Record lifecycle: clear the record on 'done' and on every block; keep it on 'retry'.

6. Append one line per settle to the iterations log (`tempFilePath(dataDir, 'iterations.log')`), e.g. `Settle #<id>: <verdict> (<reason>)`.

EXIT-CODE CONTRACT (implement the error types here; the CLI in task 99 maps them): exit 0 for every verdict, including blocked and already-settled; non-zero only when settle itself cannot run — unreadable tasks.json after repair/recovery (TasksFileError), lock timeout (FileLockError), unknown task id (SettleError).

  retry/fresh → `Launch a fresh cairn-task-agent with the same prompt file, then run: cairn round settle <id>`.

- Mapping (in order): guard block → blocked (reason = guard note); re-read status
  'blocked' → blocked (reason = task notes, fallback text if empty); failed validation

  retry 'incomplete' (continue at incompletes 1, fresh at 2); complete → done (no

If the gate does not pass: clear the record and return `done` with reason 'review-disabled' | 'no-before-sha' | 'no-commits'.
2. If the gate passes: set the record's phase to 'awaiting-review', write the reviewer prompt file, and return `{ verdict: 'review', taskId, reviewPromptFile, next }`, where next says: launch the post-task-reviewer agent with the prompt 'Read <reviewPromptFile> and follow it', then run `cairn round settle <id> --reviewed`.

     (the iteration the round would end on if each remaining task took one attempt; rounds have no cap). prevNotes = null.

# Task #99: Register the cairn round command group (next, settle) in the CLI

## TDD
Appended failing tests first to the existing test/commands/round.test.ts (`roundNextCommand`,
`roundSettleCommand`, `registerRoundCommands` describe blocks) and to test/index.test.ts (`round`
registration + settle's documented options). Ran `bun test test/commands/round.test.ts` and watched it
fail with `SyntaxError: Export named 'roundSettleCommand' not found`, then implemented until green.

## src/commands/round.ts
- `roundNextCommand({ projectRoot, dataDir, config, agents, stdout?, stderr? }, deps: RoundNextDeps = {})`
  → `Promise<number>`. Calls `roundNext`, writes its result as one JSON line to stdout, returns 0. Any
  thrown error (TasksFileError, FileLockError, etc.) is caught, written as one line to stderr
  (`cairn round next: <message>`), returns 1.
- `roundSettleCommand({ id, reviewed?, beforeSha?, testTimeoutSec?, projectRoot, dataDir, config,
  tasksFilePath?, stdout?, stderr? }, deps: Partial<SettleTaskDeps> = {})` → `Promise<number>`.
  - Validates `id` is a positive integer before doing anything else — invalid id exits 1, settle never runs.
  - Validates `testTimeoutSec` (when given) is a positive integer; converts to `timeoutMs` for
    `validateTaskTests`. The conversion wraps *whichever* `validateTaskTests` is in play — the real one or
    an injected test double — so overriding the dep never silently drops `--test-timeout`.
  - Builds a full `SettleTaskDeps` with real defaults (`defaultValidateTaskTests`,
    `defaultArchiveCompletedTasks`, `defaultGitAccess`, `defaultWriteReviewPromptFile`, `fs.existsSync`,
    `readTasksFile`, a new local `defaultBlockTask` (mirrors `commands/run.ts`'s inline one, routed through
    `mutateTasksFile`), `fs.appendFileSync`, `loadCompletedIds`), each overridable via `deps` for tests.
  - `log` defaults to a closure that writes to `stderr`, not `console.log` — this is what keeps settle's own
    log lines (e.g. "test validation errored ... settling anyway") off stdout.
  - Calls `settleTask`, writes `JSON.stringify(result.verdict)` as one line to stdout, returns 0 for every
    verdict including 'blocked' and 'already-settled'. Any thrown error (TasksFileError, FileLockError,
    SettleError) is caught → one-line stderr message, return 1.
- `defaultBlockTask` (module-private): same behavior as `commands/run.ts`'s inline `blockTask` default —
  not exported from run.ts, so duplicated here rather than reaching into run.ts's `defaultDeps()` internals.
- `loadRoundContext()` (module-private): resolves `projectRoot`/`dataDir` from `CAIRN_PROJECT_ROOT`/
  `CAIRN_DATA_DIR` (set by `setupProjectContext`'s `preAction` hook), `loadConfig` + `autoDetectHealthCheck`
  for config, and `agents` from `CAIRN_AGENTS_JSON` (same pattern as `index.ts`'s existing `run` and `plan`
  actions). Shared by both `round next` and `round settle`'s command actions.
- `registerRoundCommands(program)`: wires `round next` (no args/options) and
  `round settle <id> [--reviewed] [--before-sha <sha>] [--test-timeout <seconds>]`, each action calling its
  handler then `process.exit(code)` — mirrors `registerTaskCommands` in `src/commands/task.ts`.

## src/index.ts
- Imports and calls `registerRoundCommands(program)` right after `registerTaskCommands(program)` in
  `createProgram()`.

## src/settle.ts
- No changes needed — `SettleError`, `defaultGitAccess`, `settleTask`, `SettleTaskDeps`, `BlockTaskOpts`,
  `writeReviewPromptFile` were already exported (some from task 91-97, `defaultGitAccess` already existed).

## Exit code contract (verified against the spec)
- 0 for every settle/next verdict, including 'blocked' and 'already-settled'.
- 1 only when settle/next itself couldn't run: TasksFileError, FileLockError, SettleError (unknown task
  id), or CLI-level validation failure (invalid id, invalid --test-timeout) — always a single stderr line,
  never anything on stdout.

## Verification
- `bun test test/commands/round.test.ts test/index.test.ts`: 70 pass (38 in round.test.ts covering every
  verdict type, every error type, invalid id/timeout, the timeoutMs conversion, and the stdout-is-clean-JSON

tasks.title: cairn hook pre-tool-use: agent_type-aware containment hook (fail-open, logged)
tasks.description:
Implement `cairn hook pre-tool-use`: a Claude Code PreToolUse hook (JSON on stdin) that mechanically contains subagents under /cairn-run.

CONTEXT: under /cairn-run, subagents follow the interactive session's permission mode (recommended: bypassPermissions), so per-agent --allowedTools scoping doesn't apply and agent frontmatter can't express path scopes. Probe results from a throwaway repo with interactive `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`:
- Main-session tool calls have NO `agent_id` and NO `agent_type` keys (absent, not null). Subagent calls carry `agent_id` plus `agent_type`: 'general-purpose' for the built-in, the agent's frontmatter `name` for custom agents (e.g. 'post-task-reviewer').
- An internal Claude Code helper also fires the hook: a Bash call (`printf 'wait for it'`) with an `agent_id` but NO `agent_type` key. A missing agent_type is normal, not an error.
- Input also includes hook_event_name, permission_mode (e.g. bypassPermissions), tool_name, tool_input, cwd, session_id, transcript_path, tool_use_id.
- Hook denies bind even under bypass mode. Exit 2 shows the agent `PreToolUse:Write hook error: [<script>]: <stderr>`; exit 0 with stdout JSON `{ hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: <reason> } }` shows only the reason. USE THE JSON FORM.
- Any other failure (exit 1, or a missing binary with exit 127) lets the call through SILENTLY.

DECISION FUNCTION (pure, exported; e.g. src/hook-policy.ts or inside src/commands/hook.ts): `decidePreToolUse(input, ctx)` returning `{ decision: 'allow' }` or `{ decision: 'deny', reason }`, where ctx holds the resolved tasksFilePath, reviewsDir and projectRoot.
- Fast path: no `agent_id` → allow immediately (main session, generate-tasks, and every headless `cairn run` agent — the hook is a no-op for them). tool_name not Edit/Write/Bash → allow.
- Rule 1: any subagent (agent_id present, agent_type or not) calling Edit or Write whose tool_input.file_path resolves (relative paths against input.cwd) to the tasks.json path → deny, with a reason pointing to the `cairn task` subcommands.
- Rule 2: only when agent_type === 'post-task-reviewer' exactly: Edit/Write allowed only for paths inside the resolved reviews dir; Bash allowed only when every subcommand (split on &&, ||, ;, |, & and newlines, as buildCommandRules in src/claude-settings.ts documents) starts with one of the prefixes derived from the exported GIT_INSPECTION_RULES (e.g. 'git diff') — derive them from that list, do not duplicate it. Anything else from the reviewer → deny with a reason.
- Everything else → allow (print nothing, exit 0).

CLI: register a `hook` command group with `pre-tool-use` in src/index.ts.
- FAST STARTUP: the hook fires on every Edit/Write/Bash call in every session in the project. index.ts's preAction runs setupProjectContext (loadConfig, discoverAgents, possibly `git rev-parse`) — skip that for the hook command (e.g. check the action command's name in the preAction hook). Resolve only what is needed, lazily, after the fast path: project root from input.cwd via findProjectRoot, data dir via findDataDir (never BRAND.dataDir directly), reviews dir = <dataDir>/reviews, tasks file = <dataDir>/tasks.json.
- FAIL OPEN, VISIBLY: on any internal error (unparseable stdin, data dir not found, malformed cairn.json, any unexpected exception) never print a deny and NEVER exit 2; exit 1 and append a timestamped error line to the hook-error log `tempFilePath(dataDir, 'hook_errors.log')` — i.e. `.cairn_hook_errors.log` — whenever a data dir can be found (swallow failures writing the log). - `src/commands/hook.ts` (new):
  - `decidePreToolUse(input, ctx)` — pure policy. Fast path `isFastPathAllow`: `agent_id == null` or
    tool not Edit/Write/Bash → allow. Rule 1: any subagent Edit/Write whose file_path (resolved against
    input.cwd, falling back to ctx.projectRoot) === ctx.tasksFilePath → deny with a `cairn task` reason.

    (path.relative, so `reviews-evil/` and `..` escapes are denied); Bash only when every subcommand
    matches a GIT_INSPECTION_RULES prefix (`cmd === p || cmd.startsWith(p + ' ')`, so `git difftool` is
    denied). EXTRA beyond spec: reviewer commands containing backtick, `<`, `>` or `$(` are denied —
    `git diff > f` / `git diff $(rm x)` start with an allowed prefix but have side effects. Empty command
    → deny.
  - `preToolUseHookCommand({ stdinText, cwd?, stdout?, stderr? })` → exit code. Resolves project root /

  `actionCommand.parent?.name() === 'hook'` → no loadConfig/discoverAgents/git; a malformed cairn.json

  `warnings: ['Hook errors logged in <path> (<n> lines) — the /cairn-run containment hook may not be

tasks.title: /cairn-run slash command (commands/cairn-run.md)
tasks.description:
Write the `/cairn-run` slash command at `commands/cairn-run.md`. The repo-root commands/ directory is copied into projects' .claude/commands/ by installSlashCommands (src/commands/init.ts); do not hand-edit .claude/commands/.

CONTEXT: /cairn-run runs a full Cairn round from an interactive Claude Code session (reachable from a phone via Remote Control) instead of headless `cairn run`. The session is the RUN AGENT; all deterministic logic is in the CLI:
- `cairn round next` prints JSON: `{ verdict: 'task', taskId, title, iteration, model, promptFile, next }` | `{ verdict: 'review', taskId, reviewPromptFile, next }` | `{ verdict: 'round-done', blocked, next }`, optionally with `warnings`.
- `cairn round settle <id> [--reviewed]` prints a JSON verdict: `retry` (mode 'continue' | 'fresh', reason, failure tail), `review` (reviewPromptFile), `blocked` (reason), `done`, `already-settled`. Every verdict has a `next` hint. Exit 0 for all verdicts; non-zero means the command itself failed.
- Task agents: subagent_type `cairn-task-agent` (maxTurns 150), return at most 5 lines. Reviewer: subagent_type `post-task-reviewer`, returns one line (PASS or CONCERNS).
Read src/commands/round.ts and src/settle.ts to match the actual JSON fields before writing.

THE COMMAND FILE must instruct the run agent to:
1. Loop: run `cairn round next` and act on the verdict. For `task`: launch the Agent tool with subagent_type 'cairn-task-agent', the model from the JSON, and prompt 'Read <promptFile> and follow it'; remember the returned agent id; then run `cairn round settle <taskId>`.
2. On `review` (from next or settle): launch Agent with subagent_type 'post-task-reviewer' and prompt 'Read <reviewPromptFile> and follow it', then run `cairn round settle <taskId> --reviewed`.
3. On `retry` with mode 'continue': SendMessage to the same task agent id with the reason/failure, asking it to finish, then settle again. If the agent id is unknown (e.g. after compaction or resume), fall back to a fresh cairn-task-agent with the same prompt file. Mode 'fresh': launch a new cairn-task-agent with the same prompt file, then settle.
4. On `blocked`: send a PushNotification (task id + reason) and continue the loop — never pause with AskUserQuestion.
5. On `round-done`: send a PushNotification with a short summary, then stop.
6. On any non-zero exit from a `cairn round` command: send a PushNotification with the stderr line and STOP.
7. Surface `warnings` from next (e.g. hook errors) to the user once.
8. Rules: agents run one at a time, never in parallel and never nested (the task agent must not launch the reviewer); the run agent NEVER reads tasks.json, diffs or test logs itself and never edits tasks.json; always follow each command's `next` hint so a compacted, resumed or fresh session behaves the same; keep its own messages terse so a round of up to ~20 tasks fits without relying on compaction.
9. A permission-mode note (the command cannot set the mode): recommend launching the session in bypassPermissions — the PreToolUse hook seeded by `cairn init` (`cairn hook pre-tool-use`) still denies subagent edits to tasks.json and scopes the reviewer, and hook denies bind under bypass; `auto` mode can be tried, but its classifier may wrongly deny routine actions (git commit, bun test, cairn task); default/acceptEdits will stall an unattended round on permission prompts.
10. Frontmatter with a description, following the format of commands/generate-tasks.md and commands/review-tasks.md.

TESTS (test/commands/init.test.ts): installSlashCommands with a cairnRoot override pointing at this repo root and a temp project dir installs cairn-run.md; a content test asserts the file mentions `cairn round next`, `cairn round settle`, `--reviewed`, `cairn-task-agent`, `post-task-reviewer`, SendMessage, PushNotification and bypassPermissions.
